2314280.title: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)
2314280.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)
“When a Skill Opens Another Path”
Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 12:11PM by PIB Delhi

In villages where a family's future depends largely on harvests, acquiring a skill can often open up alternate livelihood pathways. For many rural youth, that path begins with an opportunity to learn, work, and build new sources of earning. That is where the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) enters the story. Launched on 25 September 2014 under the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), DDU-GKY focuses on youth from marginalized and vulnerable rural households. It provides placement-linked skill training aimed at sustainable livelihoods. The programme targets youth aged 15 to 35 years, linking skill training with employment opportunities.

The programme is also changing with the world of work. The revised DDU-GKY 2.0 framework places greater emphasis on industry-led training, sustainable employment, post-placement support, upskilling and reskilling. An end-to-end digital system now covers training, assessment, certification, monitoring and employment tracking. It also strengthens employer engagement through partnerships, job fairs, campus placements and industry consultations.

The focus is clear: training should lead to work, and work should have a better chance of lasting. As of June 2026, 18.45 lakh rural youth have been trained under DDU-GKY, while 12.35 lakh have been placed.

Behind these numbers are stories of individuals whose lives changed when learning opened pathways to employment and livelihoods.

Keeping the Dream Alive

For years, Vimethano Sakhrie from Nagaland witnessed her mother work tirelessly to support a family of ten. After completing high school, Vimethano aspired to pursue higher education, but financial constraints made it difficult to realise that ambition.

Everything changed when she learnt about DDU-GKY. Refusing to give up on her dreams, she enrolled in a DDU-GKY tourism and hospitality training programme. Months later, Vimethano walked into her first job at The Den Bengaluru in Food & Beverage Service. It was more than employment. It marked the beginning of a new chapter for her and her family.

Looking back on her journey, Vimethano says, "I extend my gratitude to the Ministry of Rural Development and NSRLM, Government of Nagaland for implementing DDU-GKY, which has helped many unemployed youths across India. This opportunity was a blessing for me, and I hope many more youths can benefit from it, just like I did."

For Vimethano, DDU-GKY turned an interrupted education into a launchpad for a career. For Chandan Shah, the opportunity eventually led much further from home.

From Odd Jobs to a Career Abroad

There was a time when even basic necessities were difficult for Chandan Shah's family. Living in Tetahli village of Siwan, Bihar, he had little hope of continuing his education. He left school after high school to help his father in the fields. With few opportunities around him, Chandan took up odd jobs to earn a living. Yet, the work barely offered enough for a decent life.

A new possibility emerged through his mother, who was part of the Genda JEEViKA Self Help Group. She encouraged him to explore DDU-GKY. Chandan underwent counselling and chose to train as an Assistant Electrician. The training equipped him with the skills needed to take his first step towards a career. Upon completing the course, he secured his first job in Baddi as a helper at a distillery, earning ₹10,500 per month. This early experience provided him with a foundation for further professional growth. Building on these skills and experience, Chandan later pursued an opportunity overseas and moved to Dubai, where he joined Al Shafa General Contracting as an electrician.

By then, his monthly earnings had increased to ₹35,000. The impact extended beyond his own career, bringing greater financial security to his family. Chandan was able to support his family and contribute towards his siblings’ education in private schools. His journey also made him a source of inspiration for young people in his village.

Chandan’s story illustrates how a first employment opportunity can become a foundation for sustained livelihood progression. DDU-GKY equipped him with the skills to take that first step, while his determination and experience enabled him to pursue further opportunities. Together, they helped him build a more secure future for himself and his family.

Yet, not every DDU-GKY journey leads away from home. For Rupali Hasda, the opportunity eventually brought her back.

Turning a Job into an Enterprise

Financial hardship had forced Rupali Hasda of Charaideo, Assam, to leave school after Class 9. Her family depended on agriculture, with her father as the sole earner. Her mother, an active member of a Self-Help Group, continued to encourage her dreams. Rupali learnt about DDU-GKY through a Jeevika Sakhi and enrolled in the Sewing Machine Operator trade in December 2022.

After completing her training, she secured a job at KPR Apparels Mills in Tiruppur, Tamil Nadu. For five months, she worked in an unfamiliar city and adapted to a new environment. Yet, her thoughts remained close to home. She returned to Hatibandha with savings from her job and invested Rs.50,000 in a Sewing and Cutting Centre. What began as a livelihood for herself soon created an opportunity for someone else. She employed a young girl at the centre and began building an enterprise within her community. With an annual income of around Rs.1.10 lakh, Rupali's journey shows another side of skilling. A job gave her a start, but she chose to turn that experience into something of her own.

Rupali chose to build her livelihood close to home. Hiralal, however, sought a different path-one that would enable him to build a career while navigating the challenges before him.

A Career of His Own

Hiralal Pandit from Jharkhand had grown up watching every harvest decide how far his family's money would stretch. His family of four depended on his father's seasonal farming, which earned around Rs.5,000 a month.

After completing Class 10, he began helping his father in whatever ways he could. As a differently abled young man, finding work was far from easy. but Hiralal refused to let his circumstances define his future.

He aspired to build a career of his own while contributing to the financial well-being of his family. While exploring his options, Hiralal came to know about DDU-GKY. The programme’s free training and placement support offered him an opportunity to acquire skills and pursue employment. He enrolled in the Healthcare Multipurpose trade at a training centre in Dumka, Jharkhand.

The training marked a significant turning point in Hiralal’s journey. He acquired new skills in a supportive and inclusive learning environment where he was treated with dignity and equality. After completing the course, he secured placement at SMBT Hospital in Nashik as a General Duty Assistant. The opportunity enabled him to earn independently while contributing to his family’s well-being. More importantly, the experience strengthened his confidence and broadened his sense of what he could achieve.

Today, Hiralal encourages other young people to look beyond their circumstances and make the most of the opportunities available to them. For him, the journey began with the courage to take the first step. DDU-GKY helped him turn that first step into a pathway towards a career and a more secure future.

When a Skill Becomes a Livelihood

A skill cannot remove every hardship faced by a rural household, but it can open doors to greater possibilities. For Vimethano, it provided a route to employment when financial constraints interrupted her educations. For Chandan, it marked the beginning of a career that eventually took him to Dubai. Rupali brought her skills and experience back home to build an enterprise of her own, while Hiralal found an avenue to employment and an opportunity to support his family.

Their journeys took different directions, but they share a common thread: the chance to acquire skills, apply them, and build a livelihood. DDU-GKY seeks to make that first step possible, helping rural youth move from training to employment and from employment towards more secure and sustainable livelihoods.

2314249.title: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana 2.0
2314249.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana 2.0
Building a Skilled and Self-Reliant Workforce
Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 10:47AM by PIB Delhi

 

Equipping rural youth with relevant skills and access to employment opportunities is central to advancing inclusive and sustainable rural transformation. To advance this goal, the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) was launched on 25 September 2014 under the National Rural Livelihoods Mission. Building on this, the DDU-GKY 2.0 scheme is currently being implemented across 31 States and Union Territories through over 749 approved projects, with more than 760 active training centers and over 455 Project Implementing Agencies, covering all sectors of the economy as on date. Since inception in 2014-15, more than 18.47 lakh candidates have been trained for more than 800 job roles, and over 12.43 lakh have been placed. Complementing the skilling efforts, RSETIs promote self-employment and rural entrepreneurship. As of date, 647 RSETIs across 634 districts have trained 63.47 lakh candidates, with 45.60 lakh successfully settled. These initiatives strengthen industry-aligned training, digital delivery, employment retention, and sustainable livelihood opportunities for rural youth.

 

Strengthening Rural Youth through Skills and Opportunities

India’s young population presents a significant opportunity to strengthen economic growth and rural livelihoods. The youth population is projected to reach nearly 345 million by 2036. Harnessing this demographic potential requires greater access to quality skills, employment, and livelihood opportunities.

Recognizing this need, the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) launched the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) on 25 September 2014, under the National Rural Livelihoods Mission. As DDU-GKY marks its 12th anniversary this year, the programme continues to strengthen pathways from skills to employment and sustainable livelihoods for rural youth. For more than a decade, the scheme has been providing placement-linked skill training to rural youth aged 15-35 years from poor households.

It also promotes social inclusion through mandatory coverage of SC/ST communities (50%), women (33%), and persons with disabilities (5%). Over the past decade, the scheme has evolved to place greater emphasis on employment outcomes and post-placement support. The Government notified the upgraded DDU-GKY 2.0 Guidelines in May 2025, strengthening the framework around training, placements, employment sustainability, and post-placement support. The revised framework provides training across multiple sectors based on industry requirements, including aerospace and aviation, agriculture, beauty and wellness, green jobs, healthcare, textiles, and others. The continued focus on rural skilling is also reflected in the Union Budget 2026–27, which has allocated ₹750 crore to DDU-GKY.

Special Initiatives: Targeted Interventions for Vulnerable Regions

Two special programmes are being implemented under DDU-GKY 2.0:

Roshni: It addresses the specific needs of Left-Wing Extremism (LWE)-affected districts notified by the Ministry of Home Affairs. It mandates residential skill training, with 40% coverage for women candidates. The initiative has been extended to Aspirational Districts, focusing on local infrastructure, education, health, natural resources, and traditional skills.

Himayat: It is a special DDU-GKY scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. It covers rural and urban youth, including BPL and APL persons, and supports wage, self, and gig employment. The scheme is 100% centrally funded and implemented with State support through dedicated Mission Management Units.

North East: Acknowledging the challenges in terms of socio-cultural differences and topography unique to the North Eastern States, out of the total allocation for DDU-GKY, 10% is earmarked for the North-Eastern States.

Hard to reach Areas: Further there is provision for Special Area Allowance where Project implementing agencies shall be eligible for a payment at the rate of an additional 10% of the Base training cost per candidate.

DDU-GKY 2.0: A Shift Towards Sustainable Employment

DDU-GKY 2.0 adopts a more end-to-end approach to skilling and employment, covering the journey from training and placement to employment retention and career progression.

The revised framework strengthens training standards, extends the minimum placement duration, and enhances post-placement support. It also addresses the challenges associated with migration and strengthens technology-enabled monitoring and implementation.

Standardising Training Framework

DDU-GKY 2.0 retains the 576-hour minimum while providing a more structured training framework. A three-month course comprises 396 hours of domain training and 180 hours of mandatory non-domain training. The non-domain component is standardised across four areas: English Communication (60 hours), Employability and Life Skills (60 hours), Computer and Digital Literacy (30 hours), and Entrepreneurship (30 hours). It ensures that candidates receive job-specific technical skills alongside communication, workplace, digital, and entrepreneurial capabilities.

Placement Duration

Earlier, DDU-GKY placement was defined as continuous employment for a minimum of three months. Building on this stronger training foundation, under DDU-GKY 2.0, the minimum placement duration has been extended to six months. The revised guidelines cover both continuous and non-continuous employment, including wage, self-employment, and gig employment.

Job Melas for Connecting Rural Youth with Employers

Job Melas are organised by SRLMs at the block and Gram Panchayat levels to connect local youth with potential employers. They include youth registration and counselling, employer verification, and tracking of placement outcomes for one year through Kaushal Panjee. The Melas are mainly for youth with employable skills, including DDU-GKY-trained candidates seeking better job opportunities. Funding of up to ₹50,000 per GP-level fair and ₹1 lakh per block-level fair is available from the DDU-GKY budget, subject to placement of 100 and 200 candidates, respectively.

Strengthening Employment Retention and Career Progression

Under DDU-GKY 2.0, greater emphasis has been placed on sustained employment. To support the extended six-month placement duration, DDU-GKY 2.0 provides 12 months of post-placement tracking to facilitate employment continuity, specifically:

  • Placed candidates receive financial assistance of ₹7,620, at ₹1,270 per month for six months.
  • In addition, retention support of ₹5,000 per candidate is provided to candidates who remain employed for 365 days, with a maximum employment break of 60 days.
  • Placed candidates are also provided with upskilling and reskilling opportunities after 12 months of placement, enabling them to strengthen their skills and improve their prospects for continued employment and career progression.

Migration Support Centres (MSC)

Given that a considerable proportion of trained candidates migrate in search of livelihood opportunities, DDU-GKY 2.0 has placed renewed emphasis on strengthening migration support systems. State Rural Livelihoods Missions (SRLMs) establish Migration Support Centres (MSCs) in areas with a high concentration of placed candidates. These centres operate both within the home state and in destination states. MSCs offer a range of services to support candidates during this transition, including accommodation assistance, counselling, and placement support.

They also facilitate the flow of employment-related information, encourage alumni networking, and strengthen engagement with employers. Beyond this, the centres liaise with local administrative bodies and service providers to help candidates settle into urban work environments and remain in stable employment over time. Reflecting the growing importance of this support system, per-centre annual funding for MSCs has been increased considerably, from ₹10 lakh earlier to as much as ₹30 lakh under the revised framework.

Employing Technology in Implementation

Technology integration has been a defining feature of DDU-GKY since its inception. The framework relies on geo-tagged and time-stamped biometric attendance records, computer labs, and e-learning facilities. These measures strengthened programme monitoring while enhancing trainees' exposure to digital tools.

DDU-GKY 2.0 builds upon this technological foundation by introducing an end-to-end digital solution encompassing the entire programme lifecycle. The platform spans PIA onboarding, project submission and evaluation, training-centre and candidate management, assessment and certification, financial management, and project monitoring and placement tracking.

The revised approach also introduces:

  • Advanced dashboards for real-time programme monitoring.
  • Public candidate portal for training search and viewing PIA performance ratings.
  • Automated processes, including Project Registration Number (PRN) generation, grievance redressal, and certificate verification.
  • Digital attendance and assessment through face authentication and real-time dashboards.
  • Skill India Digital Hub integration for automated course-detail validation.

Leading the Rollout (2025-26) of DDU-GKY 2.0

  • Goa has emerged as the pioneer in creating batches of DDU GKY 2.0.
  • Andhra Pradesh has commenced training of more than 12000 candidates in a short span of 3 months.
  • Jammu & Kashmir allocated 100% targets allocated and commenced trainings for 91% of the allocation.

 

Key Milestones Achieved Under the Scheme

DDU-GKY is currently being implemented across 31 States & Union Territories through an extensive skilling network. As on date, the programme has 749 approved projects, with 760 active training centres, in partnership with more than 455 PIAs.

Since its inception in 2014-15, DDU-GKY has trained over 18.47 lakh candidates, covering all 36 sectors of the economy and over 800 job roles, and placed over 12.43 lakh. This reflects the scheme’s wide sectoral reach and focus on industry-aligned skill development for rural youth.

Over 9.71 lakh women were trained, and over 6.34 lakh women secured placements under the scheme.

Other Initiatives Supporting Rural Youth Entrepreneurship

While DDU-GKY focuses on placement-linked wage employment, the Government has simultaneously strengthened self-employment and entrepreneurship pathways through Rural Self-Employment Training Institutes (RSETIs). The programme provides free residential training to rural unemployed youth aged 18-50 years, followed by handholding support for setting up sustainable livelihoods. The programme creates dedicated skill infrastructure in every district of the country. It focuses on upskilling rural youth, especially those from below poverty line (BPL) and DAY-NRLM households.

As on date, a total of 647 RSETIs are operational across 634 districts in 33 States/UTs. Since its inception (2009), the scheme has trained 63.47 lakh candidates. Total of 45.60 lakh candidates have also been settled. Among the candidates settled under RSETI, around 94% have established sustainable self-employment ventures. About 6% have secured wage employment.

 

Shaping Rural India’s Workforce for the Future

Strengthening the skills, employability, and entrepreneurship potential of rural youth remains central to inclusive economic growth in India. Through DDU-GKY 2.0, the Government is creating a more responsive, technology-driven, and outcome-oriented skilling ecosystem. The programmes prepare rural youth for jobs and support sustained livelihoods. Continued focus on quality training, industry partnerships and responsive support can help translate skills into durable livelihoods. DDU-GKY 2.0 represents an important step towards building a skilled, empowered, and self-reliant rural workforce for the future. It also promotes India’s vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 that aims to transform the country into a global economic and knowledge hub.

2314246.title: From Files to Freedom: DEPwD Sets the Stage to Turn Pendency into Productivity and Waste into Resource
2314246.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Files to Freedom: DEPwD Sets the Stage to Turn Pendency into Productivity and Waste into Resource
Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 10:29AM by PIB Delhi

From clearing pending matters to reclaiming office space, from digitizing records to responsibly disposing of e-waste, the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD) is gearing up to make Special Campaign 6.0 a focused drive for cleaner workplaces, faster disposal of pendency and more efficient governance. The campaign, being undertaken from 2nd to 31st October 2026, will give special emphasis to the effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste, while institutionalizing Swachhata across the Department and its organizations.

Launched by the Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DARPG), Special Campaign 6.0 seeks to institutionalize Swachhata and minimize pendency in Government offices. The campaign is being implemented in two phases, with the Preparatory Phase from 16th to 30th September 2026, followed by the Implementation Phase from 2nd to 31st October 2026.

DEPwD has already put in place the institutional mechanism for the campaign. A Nodal Officer has been nominated for the Department, while all Subordinate and Attached Offices, Public Sector Undertakings and Autonomous Bodies under the administrative control of DEPwD have been advised to nominate their respective Nodal Officers and identify pending matters in accordance with the parameters prescribed by DARPG.

The Department is building on the momentum generated during Special Campaign 5.0, held from 2nd to 31st October 2025, when DEPwD and its organizations achieved the targets set for the campaign. During the month-long drive, 11,972 physical files/documents were digitized and weeded out, approximately 15,588 square feet of office space was freed, and revenue of ₹14,47,619 was generated. As many as 64 cleanliness campaigns, covering indoor and outdoor spaces, were also organized by the Department and its organizations across the country.

The effort, however, did not end with the conclusion of the campaign. In keeping with the guidelines of DARPG, DEPwD and its organizations have continued to undertake Swachhata and pendency-reduction activities every month since November 2025. The achievements have also been regularly uploaded on the Special Campaign 6.0 Portal (SCDPM), reflecting the Department’s emphasis on sustained action rather than a one-time cleanliness exercise.

Special Campaign 6.0 will further reinforce this approach by bringing together the twin objectives of Swachhata and good governance—reducing avoidable pendency, improving record management, freeing up usable space and ensuring responsible disposal of obsolete material, particularly e-waste. The campaign will seek to convert idle records, redundant material and pending matters into opportunities for greater efficiency, accountability and productivity.

DEPwD is committed to making Special Campaign 6.0 a meaningful and outcome-oriented exercise. Concerted efforts will be undertaken by the Department and its organizations to achieve the targets identified during the preparatory phase and to carry forward the culture of cleanliness, timely disposal and efficient use of public resources as an integral part of everyday governance.

2314239.title: PBSHABD
2314239.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
PBSHABD
Prasar Bharati's Trusted News for India’s Newsrooms
Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 10:13AM by PIB Delhi

PBSHABD is the free news feed service of Prasar Bharati, India's public service broadcaster. Launched in March 2024, it serves as a news wire for the wider media industry. Registered organisations may draw text, video, audio, photographs and infographics in 15 Indian languages. The service is free up to March 2027 and serves 3,600 media organisations. Its content is gathered through a nationwide network and verified through multiple layers of editorial checks. PBSHABD thereby extends the reach of credible information across India's media landscape.

 

From PBNS to PBSHABD: Evolution of a Public News Service

Prasar Bharati is India's public service broadcaster and an autonomous body created by an Act of Parliament. It came into existence on 23 November 1997 under the Prasar Bharati Act, 1990. The corporation works through two constituents, Akashvani and Doordarshan. Its mandate is a fair and balanced flow of information in the public interest.

News gathering has always been central to this mandate. The Prasar Bharati News Service (PBNS) began as a news wire strictly for the broadcaster's own editorial teams. Its copy and feeds supported bulletins across Akashvani and Doordarshan. At that stage, the service remained an internal newsroom resource.

The scope of the service was enlarged in March 2024. The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MIB) launched PBSHABD on 13 March 2024 in New Delhi. The service now carries the name Prasar Bharati – Shared Audio-Visuals for Broadcast and Dissemination. It gives registered media organisations free, ready-to-use news in text, video, audio, photo and infographic formats. An internal news wire thus became an open multimedia news-sharing platform. The table below traces the main milestones of this journey.

 

Year

Milestone

1990

Parliament enacts the Prasar Bharati Act.

1997

The corporation comes into existence on 23 November 1997.

Till 2024

PBNS works as an internal news wire for Prasar Bharati's editorial teams.

March 2024

PBSHABD is launched on 13 March as a free, multi-format news-sharing platform.

March 2025

Free access is extended to March 2026 on completion of one year.

March 2026

Free access is extended further, up to March 2027.

Ahead

PBSHABD 2.0 is planned, with new product lines and improved delivery.

 

PBSHABD is not a newsroom built from scratch. It is an extension of news infrastructure developed over several decades. The same correspondents, desks and bureaux now serve a far wider set of users. The reach of the content has changed, while the editorial foundation has stayed the same. How that reach works is best understood through the design of the service itself.

Did You Know?

The name of the service carries two meanings. It expands to Shared Audio-Visuals for Broadcast and Dissemination. In Hindi, the word shabd means the spoken or written word. The platform was built to share that word widely, quickly and free of cost.

PBSHABD: A Multi-Format, Multilingual News Feed

PBSHABD is a news feed service of Prasar Bharati, open to media users round the clock. It supplies timely, authentic and ready-to-use news content from India and the world. The feed carries developments as they occur, from the national capital to district headquarters.

Its users are registered media organisations, digital publishers and content creators. Newspapers, news television channels and digital news publishers form the bulk of this base. In two years of operation, the service has built a user base of 3,600 media organisations.

Content is offered in five formats, namely text, video, audio, photographs and infographics.  News is provided in 15 Indian languages and under nearly 50 news categories. Coverage extends across national, regional and local developments. The service is free of cost. Registered users pay no subscription fee for the content they download. Free access has been assured up to March 2027. Read More About Features & Benefits of PBSHABD

Who can register

Registered newspapers and journals may sign up with a valid RNI certificate. Television and radio stations require valid uplink and downlink certificates. Digital publishers may register on submission of a copy of their PAN. Each organisation receives one login, which its journalists mayshare within the newsroom. Read more about PBSHABD registration here.

One Platform, Many Content Products

PBSHABD is designed as a bouquet of services rather than a single news wire. Each product is prepared for direct use by a particular kind of newsroom.

One feature sets the platform apart from a conventional news agency. Content carries no Prasar Bharati logo and needs no credit line. A small newspaper may therefore run a national story under its own masthead.

From the Ground to the Newsroom: The Network Behind PBSHABD

The strength of PBSHABD lies in the network that feeds it. Prasar Bharati runs one of the largest news gathering and desk networks in the country. More than 1,500 reporters, correspondents and stringers contribute to this pipeline. Sixty dedicated edit desks work round the clock on the material they send. Akashvani and Doordarshan run their own regional news units and bulletin services. Between them, they cover almost every State and Union Territory. The table below indicates the reach of this network.

Network

Reach on the ground

Akashvani News
  • 46 Regional News Units, 1 Headquarter
  • 607 bulletins a day in 92 languages and dialects

Doordarshan News
  • 31 Regional News Units, 1 Headquarter
  • Over 145 bulletins in more than 22 languages and dialects

Field strength
  • Over 1,500 reporters, correspondents and stringers across the country

Editorial desks
  • 60 dedicated desks working round the clock

 

Editorial checks before dissemination

News on PBSHABD passes through multiple layers of editorial checks. The service maintains firm guardrails against fake, morphed or manipulated content. It is careful with material drawn from unverified online sources. Every story is timestamped, datelined and properly captioned. Users therefore know exactly when and where a development took place. Technology widens the reach of this service. The news gathering and editorial network gives it a strong news foundation.

Accuracy, Authenticity and Timeliness: The Spirit of Public Service

Accuracy and authenticity sit at the centre of the service. Content is professionally produced, edited and verified before it is shared. The round-the-clock feed ensures that verified news reaches users without delay. Its range of formats and languages makes the service genuinely inclusive. In a crowded information environment, verified content is itself a public good.

Connecting India's Diverse Media Ecosystem

Audiences now receive news across many platforms at the same time. Television, newspapers, websites, mobile applications, YouTube and social media all carry the day's events. A newsroom must therefore publish in several formats every single day. PBSHABD connects Prasar Bharati's news gathering infrastructure with this wider ecosystem. Newspapers, television broadcasters, digital publishers, creators and platforms draw from the same feed.

The benefit is sharpest for smaller and regional organisations. A district newspaper rarely maintains correspondents in Delhi or abroad. Through PBSHABD it can access professionally produced national and international coverage. Ready-to-use text, video and audio reduce both cost and turnaround time.

The Road Ahead

PBSHABD carries Prasar Bharati's news gathering capability beyond its own channels. Credible information now travels through thousands of independent outlets. The service is positioned for steady expansion in the period ahead. Free access to the platform has been extended up to March 2027. Media organisations may therefore plan their use of the feed with certainty. The user base has risen to 3,600 media organisations in two years of operation.

Accurate news remains a public good in an age of rapid information flows. Prasar Bharati remains committed to free, fair and factual news reporting and dissemination. Every verified story on the platform strengthens the foundation of an informed citizenry. PBSHABD thus stands as shared national infrastructure for the dissemination of credible information.

2314215.title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA LAUNCHES BRAHMA KUMARIS’ CAMPAIGN ‘SPIRITUAL AWAKENING FOR WORLD RENEWAL’ AND INAUGURATES ‘GLOBAL SPIRITUAL PALACE’ RETREAT CENTRE AT VADODARA, GUJARAT
2314215.body_html:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA LAUNCHES BRAHMA KUMARIS’ CAMPAIGN ‘SPIRITUAL AWAKENING FOR WORLD RENEWAL’ AND INAUGURATES ‘GLOBAL SPIRITUAL PALACE’ RETREAT CENTRE AT VADODARA, GUJARAT
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 10:15PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu launched Brahma Kumaris’ campaign ‘Spiritual Awakening for World Renewal’ and inaugurated the ‘Global Spiritual Palace’ Retreat Centre at Vadodara, Gujarat today (September 23, 2026). On the occasion, the President also virtually launched the campaign ‘Youth for Viksit Bharat: Awakening Inner Strength for Nation Building’ of Brahma Kumaris Nadiad, Gujarat.

Addressing the gathering, the President said that today, there is a need not only for economic development but also for human development. We need an education that does not merely develop the intellect but also awakens wisdom. We need progress that is accompanied by sensitivity towards nature. We need a form of strength that teaches self-control rather than the control of others. We need spirituality that connects human beings. She was happy to note that the Brahma Kumaris organisation has spread the message of personal transformation and global renewal, through meditation and spiritual knowledge, not only across India but also to many countries around the world.

The President said that the potential for change exists within every human being. If people believe that changing their thoughts and actions can transform their life and if hope and self-respect are restored to them, they can become instruments of positive change not only for themselves but for society as a whole. She expressed confidence that today's inauguration of the Global Spiritual Palace will become a place where people from diverse sections of society can come together in peace and harmony.

The President said that it is heartening to virtually inaugurate the ‘Youth for Viksit Bharat: Awakening Inner Strength for Nation Building’ campaign at Nadiad, the birthplace of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. She said that when the youth channel their thoughts, emotions, and actions in a positive direction, the impact extends to the family, the workplace, the community, and ultimately, the entire nation. Therefore, "Awakening Inner Strength" is not merely a message of personal development but a profound process of nation-building. She emphasised that it is our collective responsibility to empower the youth. We have to transform them into self-reliant, peace-loving and responsible citizens.

The President said that self-transformation is considered the foundation of societal transformation. Today, there is a need to align this great legacy with the requirements of modern life. Our goal should be to build an India that is economically prosperous, scientifically advanced, socially inclusive, and spiritually awakened.

2314214.title: Day 2 of IIWW 2026 Brings Diverse Perspectives Together on Water Security, Innovation and Resilient WASH Services
2314214.body_html:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
Day 2 of IIWW 2026 Brings Diverse Perspectives Together on Water Security, Innovation and Resilient WASH Services
From Source Sustainability to AI-Enabled Solutions, IIWW 2026 Technical Sessions Spotlight the Future of Water Management
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 10:04PM by PIB Delhi

The second day of the 9th India International Water Week (IIWW 2026) transitioned into its full technical schedule at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, centering on the theme of climate-resilient water management. Organized by the Ministry of Jal Shakti, the day featured parallel deliberations across Country, Water Leaders', Practitioners', and Thematic Forums, alongside dedicated side events and the concurrent Second International WASH Conference.

Addressing the Netherland-led Country Forum on “Success Stories in Water Management, Food Security and Source Sustainability”, Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Shri Ashok K.K. Meena highlighted that India and the Netherlands share a common understanding that water management is not merely an engineering challenge but also a governance, community and climate-resilience challenge. He noted that India’s experience under Jal Jeevan Mission has demonstrated that water security requires strong political commitment, community ownership, scientific planning, accountable institutions and digital innovation working together. He further emphasised that the Mission’s focus is increasingly shifting from infrastructure creation to sustainability, service quality and long-term water security.

Shri Meena also highlighted the growing scope of India-Netherlands cooperation in advancing climate-resilient and sustainable water systems. He referred to initiatives such as the Sujalam Bharat Digital Public Infrastructure and Decision Support Systems for source sustainability, which support data-driven planning, asset management and risk-informed decision-making. Emphasising the importance of source sustainability, greywater management and local government ownership, he noted that India looks forward to learning from the Netherlands’ extensive experience in water governance while deepening collaboration through research, innovation, capacity building and knowledge exchange.

The technical session on “Effective Greywater Management for Rural Areas”, chaired by Ms Aishvarya Singh, Joint Secretary & Mission Director, Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), DDWS highlighted the increasing importance of greywater management in the context of expanding rural water supply coverage. The session brought together State Mission Directors, development partners, Panchayati Raj representatives and grassroots practitioners to share experiences and best practices from different parts of the country, including Andhra Pradesh, Sikkim, Bihar, Jammu & Kashmir and Jharkhand.

In her remarks, Ms Singh emphasised that there is no one-size-fits-all approach to greywater management and that solutions must be adapted to local conditions and community needs. The deliberations focused on decentralised treatment and reuse models, integration of greywater management into Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs), and strengthening community participation to ensure sustainable water and sanitation outcomes in rural areas.

On the second day of the Second International WASH Conference 2026, six technical sessions were organised on the themes of (i) Digital Technology, AI and Innovation for WASH; (ii) Governance, Community Participation and Institutional Strengthening; (iii) Climate Resilience, Nature-Based Solutions and Sanitation; (iv) Water Quality, Safety and Emerging Contaminants; (v) Financing, Economic Models and Techno-Economic Solutions; and (vi) Governance, Community Participation and Institutional Strengthening. A total of 25 technical papers were presented, showcasing innovative approaches, emerging research and practical solutions for strengthening climate-resilient and sustainable WASH services.

Technical sessions Details

The first technical session, “Digital Technology, AI & Innovation for WASH,” focused on the use of technology to strengthen the management, monitoring and maintenance of water and sanitation services. Four papers covered a digital communication and monitoring system for rural sanitation in Bihar, a low-cost IoT-based system for on-site detection of heavy metal ions, smart water meters as water-saving devices, and AI-driven decision support for predictive operation and maintenance of rural water supply systems. The presentations highlighted the potential of digital technologies, IoT and AI to improve service monitoring, efficiency and asset management.

The second technical session, “Governance, Community Participation & Institutional Strengthening,” focused on community participation, inclusive approaches and institutional collaboration for sustainable WASH services. Four papers covered a gender-inclusive sanitation model at PCMC, community ownership and digital engagement for rural piped water services in Bihar through the Dastak Abhiyan, inter-departmental collaboration for WASH through the Jal Vidya Programme in Assam, and a service-learning framework for rural sanitation. The session highlighted the role of community ownership, institutional coordination and inclusive approaches in strengthening WASH outcomes.

The third technical session, “Climate Resilience, Nature-Based Solutions & Sanitation/Other,” focused on approaches to strengthening climate resilience and sustainability across water, sanitation and waste management systems. Four papers covered climate adaptation in urban water systems, a cost-effective climate-resilient model for solid waste management, participatory village planning for greywater management, and the application of remotely operated vehicles, AI and sensor technologies for water infrastructure protection and asset management. The session highlighted the role of climate-responsive planning, community participation and technology-enabled approaches in building resilient WASH systems.

The fourth technical session, “Water Quality, Safety & Emerging Contaminants,” focused on approaches to strengthening water quality management and water safety. Five papers examined an integrated approach to safe, energy-independent rural handpump water supply, drinking water quality under the Jal Jeevan Mission in Bongaigaon, Assam, sensor-based detection of water-borne pathogens, community-scale water disinfection technologies, and the use of Jal Jeevan Mission water quality data for seasonal public health risk identification. The presentations highlighted the importance of integrated monitoring, appropriate technologies and data-driven approaches to ensuring safe drinking water.

The fifth technical session, “Financing, Economic Models & Techno-Economic Solutions,” focused on approaches to improving the financial, technological and economic sustainability of WASH services. Four papers covered tablet-based inline chlorination as a cost-effective water safety solution, sustainable approaches to river water filtration and quality assessment, innovative economic models for rural WASH and community sustainability, and the socio-economic assessment of the GOBARdhan component in rural Gujarat. The session highlighted the role of cost-effective technologies, innovative economic models and local capacity building in supporting sustainable water and sanitation services.

The sixth technical session, “Governance, Community Participation & Institutional Strengthening,” focused on community participation, local governance and resilience in WASH service delivery. Four papers examined community participation and social governance in achieving SDG 6 in Rajasthan, the performance of the Swachh Bharat Mission in rural Hoshiarpur, Punjab, approaches to strengthening institutional linkages for flood-resilient WASH systems, and the climate resilience of rural water sources in PESA areas of Himachal Pradesh. The presentations highlighted the importance of community participation, institutional linkages, and locally responsive approaches in strengthening sustainable and climate-resilient WASH systems.

Discussion moved from the opening day's high-level themes into detailed, sector-specific work, spanning water governance and equity, technology adoption and efficiency, climate risk, treated wastewater reuse and community-led recharge. The Thematic Forum opened its paper presentations, across the first three of the Forum's seven sub-themes. The sessions drew on the shortlisted papers gathered in the conference proceedings.

COUNTRY FORUM (CF)

CF-2 on Sharing Technology-Driven Initiatives in Water Security: German and EU Solutions for Sustainable Water Management in India, was chaired by Mr. Gottfried von Gemmingen, Head of Economic Cooperation & Development at the German Embassy in New Delhi, with GIZ, Siemens, Watershed Monitoring Inc., Asoti Engineering, HUBER Envirotech, and NIVUS Technologies, on digital and precision technologies for water security.

CF-3 on Success Stories of Countries in Water Management, Food Security and Source Sustainability, convened with the Netherlands and CEEW was chaired by Mr. Jaap Slootmaker, Vice-Minister of Water & Soil Affairs at the Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management, Govt. of the Netherlands and co-chaired by Shri Ashok K. K. Meena, IAS, Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India, discussed circular water economies, climate-resilient agriculture and knowledge transfer.

WATER LEADERS’ FORUM (WLF)

WLF-1 on Partnership and Cooperation for Inclusive Water Management, convened with Maharashtra and the World Bank, Drinking Water & Sanitation Department, Jharkhand; IWMI; Development Support Centre, Ahmedabad and Paani Foundation, Maharashtra, was chaired by Dr. Sanjay Belsare, Secretary (CAD), WRD, Maharashtra, and co-chaired by Shri Ajith Radhakrishnan, Senior Water Resources Management Specialist, World Bank, discussed partnership models for water access, quality and resilience across India's agro-climatic regions.

WLF-2 on Technological Solutions for Efficient Water Utilisation, convened with FICCI and chaired by Smt. Naina Lal Kidwai, Chair, FICCI Water Mission, FICCI and co-chaired by Shri Pradeep Kumar Agrawal, Joint Secretary & Chairman, Central Ground Water Authority, focused on smart irrigation, digital water management, leak detection and industrial water efficiency.

PRACTITIONERS’ FORUM (PF)

PF-1 on State Initiatives in Water Management, was chaired by the Shri Bhopal Singh, Former Member, Central Water Commission, with Shri Zaigam Ali Khan Joint Secretary, NRCD as co-chair, brought together officers and representatives from WRD, Maharashtra; Greater Chennai Corporation; NEIDA; WRD, Madhya Pradesh; and WRD, Haryana, discussed State-level interventions in conservation and service delivery.

PF-2 on Large-Scale Adoption of Water Saving and Climate-Smart Technology: Lessons from States, was chaired by Shri Eknath Dawale, IAS, Principal Secretary, WRD, Maharashtra, and Shri Sumant Narain, Joint Secretary, National Water Mission as co-chair on micro-irrigation, solar pumps and digital mapping across Maharashtra, Bihar, Karnataka and Gujarat.

PF-3 on Effective Greywater Management for Rural Areas, convened with the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation was chaired by Smt. Aishvarya Singh, JS&MD, SBM(G), DDWS and co-chaired by Shri Brijesh Pandey, Secretary, PWD, Govt. of Tripura on the 3Rs (Reduce, Recharge and Reuse) approach, with about 5.46 lakh villages now having greywater management arrangements; the panel drew in SBM(G) mission directors and grassroots Swachhagrahis and sarpanches.

PF-4 on Smart Irrigation Management, was chaired by Shri Yogesh Paithankar, Member (WP&P), Central Water Commission, and co-chaired by Shri Rajeev Kumar, Chief Engineer, UGBO, Central Water Commission. The panelists discussed remote sensing, IoT and AI in irrigation, with IWMI and technology providers.

THEMATIC FORUM (TF)

Eight Thematic Forum sessions ran through the day presenting shortlisted papers and spanning the first three of the Forum's seven sub-themes.

Sub-theme 1, Inclusive and Equitable Water Governance: TF-1 Equity in Water Allocation and Access to All Sectors, was chaired by Shri S. Masood Husain, Former Chairman, CWC, and co-chaired by Shri Vineet Gupta, Member, CWMA; TF-2 Water Governance Principles: Indicators, Audit and Standards, was chaired by Shri B. R. K. Pillai, Professor of Practice, IIT Roorkee, and co-chaired by Dr. P. Somasekhar Rao, Director (Technical), Advanced Centre for Integrated Water Resources Management, Govt. of Karnataka; and TF-3 Institutional Reforms and Strengthening was chaired by Shri Yogesh Paithankar, Member (WP&P), CWC with Shri Ashish Banerjee, Chief Engineer (IMO), CWC as co-chair. Papers examined equity-based groundwater allocation, women's participation in water governance and the Solar Didi self-help-group model, water auditing and benchmarking of irrigation projects, and parliamentary discourse on river governance.

Sub-theme 2, Collaboration for Optimal Use of Water Resources: TF-4 Treated Wastewater Reuse Across Sectors was chaired by Shri Praveen Gupta, Member (Thermal) Central Electrical Authority, with Shri Nalin Kumar Srivastava, Deputy Director General, NMCG as co-chair. TF-5 Multi-Stakeholder Partnerships for Efficient Water Management, was chaired by Shri S. K. Haldar, Chairperson, CWMA, with Shri Gopal Kumar, Country Representative, India & Bangladesh, IWMI as co-chair; and TF-6 International Collaboration in the Field of Climate-Related Risk chaired by Prof. Dr. Deepak Khare, Department of Water Resources Development & Management and co-chaired by Dr. Manish K. Nema, Scientist-E, National Institute of Hydrology, Roorkee. Papers ranged over the circular economy in wastewater, water-sensitive cities, geospatial technologies in the Ken-Betwa link, and drought and flood risk assessment, including a basin-based approach to climate resilience in Kerala.

Sub-theme 3, Technology and Community for Water Security: TF-7 Forecasting and Modelling for Water Security, was chaired by Dr. A. K. Gosain, Professor Emeritus, Department of Civil Engineering, IIT Delhi, and co-chaired by Dr. Ajai Pradhan, President & CEO, Cetus Consulting Pvt. Ltd. and TF-8 Community Participation in Groundwater Recharge, was chaired by Shri Cyril V. Darlong Diengdoh, Commissioner & Secretary, WRD, Govt. of Meghalaya and co-chaired by Dr. Dipankar Saha, Chair Professor, Center for Advanced Water Technology & Management, Manav Rachna University and Board President, Water for People. TF-7 spanned AI, machine learning and remote sensing for water security, SCADA and GIS integration, and flood modelling at river confluences; TF-8 drew on community-led desilting, spring rejuvenation, managed aquifer recharge and the Atal Bhujal Yojana.

SIDE EVENTS (SE)

SE-1 on Scaling Water-for-Food Solutions in India: Maximising the Impact of PMKSY through Finance, Partnerships and Innovation, convened by the World Bank with the International Water Management Institute (IWMI), examined how the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana can be strengthened through better financing, stronger partnerships and new innovation to make irrigation water go further for farmers. The session was chaired by Shri Pradeep Kumar Agrawal, Joint Secretary and Chairman, Central Ground Water Authority, and graced by Shri Saroj Jha, Global Director, Water Department, World Bank, who brought a global perspective on financing water security for agriculture.

SE-2 on GSDP Conversation Series: Accelerating India's Water Vision 2047 through Indo-German Cooperation, convened by the German Embassy, looked at how the India-Germany partnership can help translate India's long-term water vision for 2047 into practical action on the ground.

H. E. Jasper Wieck, Ambassador, Embassy of the Federal Republic of Germany, New Delhi, delivered the Inaugural Address. The session was also graced by the august presence of Shri Raj Bhushan Choudhary, Hon’ble Minister of State for Jal Shakti, who delivered the keynote address.

2314194.title: AIIA Celebrates 11th Ayurveda Day–2026 with Public Awareness Rally, Seminar and Book Launches
2314194.body_html:
AYUSH
AIIA Celebrates 11th Ayurveda Day–2026 with Public Awareness Rally, Seminar and Book Launches
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 9:22PM by PIB Delhi

 The All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), an autonomous organisation under the Ministry of Ayush, celebrated the 11th Ayurveda Day at its campus with a series of academic, awareness and outreach activities. Two major programmes were organised as part of the celebrations.

To mark the occasion, an “Ayurveda Public Awareness Rally” was organised in the morning with the objective of promoting Ayurveda, propagating its principles, and creating greater public awareness about the role of Ayurveda in healthy living and holistic healthcare.

Prof. (Vaidya) P.K. Prajapati, Director, AIIA, participated in the rally along with Prof. (Dr.) Manjusha Rajagopala, Dean, DU; Prof. (Dr.) Mahesh Vyas, Dean, Ph.D.; Prof. (Dr.) Ramakant Yadav, Dean, PG; Dr. Yogesh Badwe, MS; and faculty members, non-faculty members, Ph.D. and postgraduate (PG) scholars, and staff of the Institute.

In the afternoon, a seminar was organised on the theme “One Health, One Future: Integrating Science through Evidence, Innovations & Holistic Care.” Prof. (Dr.) Ravichandiran V., Vice-Chancellor, Delhi Pharmaceutical Sciences and Research University (DPSRU), was the Chief Guest at the programme. He congratulated AIIA for its efforts towards promoting Ayurveda globally and appreciated the Institute’s initiatives. Dr. Vinay Choudhary, Medical Officer, Department of AYUSH, Government of India, was the Guest of Honour. He delivered a lecture on autoimmune disorders in clinical Ayurvedic practice.

Prof. (Vaidya) Pradeep Kumar Prajapati, Director, AIIA, emphasised the importance of collective participation in Ayurveda awareness initiatives and strengthening public engagement with Ayurveda as part of the Institute’s outreach activities. Speaking on the occasion, he highlighted the various initiatives undertaken by AIIA to mark Ayurveda Day. He said, “In line with the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, One Earth, One Health, Ayurveda is today moving beyond being India’s traditional healthcare heritage to become an important part of the global health discourse. As part of these celebrations, departments have organised seminars, expert lectures, webinars, public awareness programmes and patient-centric activities on diverse aspects of Ayurveda and healthcare.”

He also informed that AIIA launched “AyurVarta,” a special talk show dedicated to Ayurveda. The Institute organised AYURPRABHA-2026, a six-day workshop on Ayurveda Dermatology and Cosmetology, and conducted a special eye-screening camp for students of an NTPC school, among several other initiatives.

Two books, “Tarangini Sara Sangraha” and “Integrative Healthcare for Better Outcomes,” were also launched on the occasion.

2314190.title: DRI seizes around 21 kg foreign-origin gold worth Rs. 32 crore in crackdown on gold smuggling
2314190.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
DRI seizes around 21 kg foreign-origin gold worth Rs. 32 crore in crackdown on gold smuggling
Seized gold smuggled from neighbouring countries; 5 persons arrested
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 9:13PM by PIB Delhi

Continuing its sustained crackdown on gold smuggling, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has seized around 21 kg foreign-origin gold in two operations, cumulatively valued at more than Rs. 61 crore in seven separate operations carried out across the country. Five persons have been arrested under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.

Based on specific intelligence, DRI officers intercepted two new Thar vehicles near Palwal Toll Plaza. The very ingenious  and sophisticated concealed cavity in the chassis of both the vehicles that had been created by removing and expertly welding back a portion of the chassis over the rear wheel proved extremely difficult to detect. Only upon  painstaking rummaging of these vehicles, DRI officers could successfully locate the concealment. A total of 15.18 kg. gold in form of bars, valued at approximately Rs. 23.30 crore was recovered from two vehicles and seized on 19.09.26. Four persons accompanying the vehicles were arrested. The intelligence indicates that the gold has been smuggled from Myanmar.

Earlier, in another operation on 16.09.26, officers of DRI intercepted a passenger at Jewar Toll Plaza, who was travelling by bus from Gorakhpur towards Delhi. Personal search led to the recovery and seizure of 5.8 kg of foreign-origin gold, comprising five 1-kg gold bars and approximately 800 grams of cut pieces, valued concealed in a specially designed cotton waist belt. The person was arrested under the Customs Act, 1962. Preliminary investigation indicated that the gold had been handed over to him in Kathmandu and brought into India through the India-Nepal land border.

In last three weeks, DRI officers have seized around 123 kg gold and around 10 kg silver, collectively valued at more than Rs 187 crore in various operations across the country. 58 persons have been arrested for smuggling gold. These operations underscore DRI’s continued focus on disrupting organised gold-smuggling networks and detecting increasingly sophisticated methods of concealment.

2314188.title: DRI seizes around 12 kg foreign-origin gold smuggled from Bangladesh worth Rs. 17 crore in a crackdown on cross border gold smuggling
2314188.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
DRI seizes around 12 kg foreign-origin gold smuggled from Bangladesh worth Rs. 17 crore in a crackdown on cross border gold smuggling
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 9:07PM by PIB Delhi

Continuing its intensified crackdown on cross-border gold smuggling, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), in coordination with the Border Security Force (BSF), has disrupted multiple consignments of foreign-origin gold smuggled through the India-Bangladesh border. In a series of operations in West Bengal and Bihar, around 12 kg foreign-origin gold, cumulatively valued at around Rs. 17 crore were recovered and seized from locations along the border as well as from a train passenger, exposing the continued use of the Bangladesh route for clandestine movement of gold into the country.

On 20-21.09.26, in West Bengal, BSF personnel of 161 BN recovered 27 pieces of   unclaimed foreign origin smuggled gold weighing around 3.15 kg near India Bangladesh Border Road in area under BOP Gongra and subsequently, DRI took up the proceedings and seized the gold under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.

In another operation on 21.09.26, BSF personnel of 161 BN at BOP Mahakhola recovered 10 pieces of 24K foreign origin smuggled gold weighing around 1.16 kg concealed near a handpump in Village Hathkhola, ahead of India Bangladesh Border Fence. Subsequently, DRI joined the recovered gold, the same was seized under the provisions of Section 110 of the Customs Act, 1962. Previously, on 10-11.09.26, foreign-origin gold comprising of 48 bars, weighing around 5.9 kg was recovered near the India-Bangladesh border fence in the BOP Pathergata area by BSF personnel, which was also taken over and seized by DRI.


In Patna, DRI officers, recovered and seized 15 gold bars and 4 tiny cut pieces of gold of foreign origin weighing around 1.71 kg from a train passenger.  The gold was concealed in cloth knee cap wrapped around both his legs. The investigations indicated that the gold had been smuggled from Bangladesh. The person has been arrested.

The operations highlight the continued efforts of DRI done in close coordination with BSF to disrupt the networks involved in the smuggling, transportation and distribution of foreign-origin gold through the Bangladesh route.

2314176.title: CCI approves acquisition of certain additional equity share capital of IIFL Capital Services Ltd by FIH Mauritius Investments Ltd.
2314176.body_html:
Competition Commission of India
CCI approves acquisition of certain additional equity share capital of IIFL Capital Services Ltd by FIH Mauritius Investments Ltd.
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 8:48PM by PIB Delhi

The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved acquisition of certain additional equity share capital of IIFL Capital Services Limited (Target) by FIH Mauritius Investments Ltd. (Acquirer).

The Proposed Combination envisages the acquisition by the Acquirer of certain issued and paid-up equity share capital of Target on a fully diluted basis. This will be undertaken in the following manner:

    1. FIHM will subscribe to certain fresh equity shares of Target by way of a preferential issue on a private placement basis.
    2. FIHM will offer to acquire certain equity shares tendered in the mandatory open offer by public shareholders of Target.
    3. The Acquirer may also undertake a secondary purchase from the promoters of the Target, if FIHM’s and HWIC’s aggregate shareholding in IIFL Capital remains less than the Target Shareholding post completion of the primary subscription and the open offer acquisition.

The Acquirer is a private company limited by shares incorporated in Mauritius. It is an investment holding company which is focused on long-term capital appreciation while preserving capital through investments in equity securities and debt instruments of Indian businesses and businesses primarily connected to India. It holds a Global Business License issued by the Financial Commission of Mauritius. It does not, however, carry out any other business activities, whether in India or globally.

FIHM is a wholly owned subsidiary of Fairfax India Holdings Corporation, a company listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange. Fairfax Financial Holdings Limited, which is the ultimate parent entity of FIHM, is a Canadian-based holding company which, through its subsidiaries, is primarily engaged in property and casualty insurance and reinsurance and associated investment management in various countries, including India.

The Target is a public limited company incorporated in India. It is a Securities and Exchange Board of India-registered financial services company which, directly and through its group companies, offers integrated solutions in wealth management, investment banking, broking services, institutional equities and research for high net-worth / ultra-high net-worth clients and family offices.

Its primary business activities comprise of stockbroking services across asset classes such as equity and commodities, investment banking and distribution of financial products in India.

2314173.title: CARI Guwahati Concludes 10-Day Celebrations of 11th Ayurveda Day
2314173.body_html:
AYUSH
CARI Guwahati Concludes 10-Day Celebrations of 11th Ayurveda Day
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 8:45PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Ayurveda Research Institute (CARI), Guwahati, concluded a 10-day series of programmes organised to mark the 11th Ayurveda Day 2026 with a public walkathon today.

Held under the theme “Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow”, the celebrations included health camps, awareness programmes, lectures, exhibitions and community outreach activities focused on preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyle practices and Ayurveda.

As part of the celebrations, CARI Guwahati organised free health check-up camps at various locations across Assam, providing medical consultations, diagnostic screenings and Ayurvedic medicines. The camps also focused on creating awareness about early intervention and preventive healthcare practices.

Awareness lectures were organised at the Institute’s OPD on various aspects of Ayurveda, including Dinacharya (daily regimen), Ritucharya (seasonal regimen) and appropriate Ahara (diet). Interactive exhibitions and awareness activities on medicinal plants were also organised to familiarise the public with their traditional uses and importance.

CARI Guwahati also conducted outreach programmes for personnel of the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) at IOCL, Bongaigaon, focusing on stress management, yoga and Ayurveda-based approaches for maintaining physical and mental well-being.

An expert seminar on Marma Chikitsa was conducted by Dr. Tikendrajit Sarma, Associate Professor, Government Ayurvedic College, Guwahati. The session provided an overview of traditional Ayurvedic approaches related to Marma points and their relevance in healthcare.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr. P. L. Bharati, Research Officer (In-charge), CARI Guwahati, highlighted the role of Ayurveda in promoting preventive healthcare and healthy living. He said that the 10-day programme was aimed at connecting Ayurvedic principles with contemporary lifestyle needs and encouraging people to adopt healthy practices in their daily lives.

The celebrations culminated in a public walkathon, which was flagged off by Mrs. Anjana Bora, Councillor, Ward No. 43, Guwahati Municipal Corporation. Healthcare professionals, youth and members of the local community participated in the event.

The 10-day celebrations provided a platform for CARI Guwahati to engage with the community through healthcare services, awareness activities and educational programmes, highlighting the preventive and promotive aspects of Ayurveda.

2314172.title: 11th Ayurveda Day Celebrated at Central Ayurveda Research Institute, New Delhi
2314172.body_html:
AYUSH
11th Ayurveda Day Celebrated at Central Ayurveda Research Institute, New Delhi
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 8:43PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Ayurveda Research Institute (CARI), New Delhi, celebrated the 11th Ayurveda Day today with a series of activities aimed at creating awareness about Ayurveda, healthy lifestyle practices and preventive healthcare.

The programme commenced with Dhanwantri Poojan, performed by Dr. Hemant Panigrahi, Institute In-charge, in the presence of officers and officials of the Institute.

As part of the celebrations, a ‘Run for Ayurveda’ was organised with participation from officers, employees and patients of the Institute. The initiative focused on promoting awareness about Ayurveda and healthy living.

An Ayurveda Day lecture was also organised, highlighting the principles of Ayurveda, healthy lifestyle practices, disease prevention and the relevance of Ayurveda in contemporary healthcare. Participants and patients were sensitised to the role of Ayurveda in health promotion and disease prevention.

Medicinal plants were distributed among patients visiting the Institute to create awareness about their importance, conservation and appropriate use.

A press conference was also organised on the occasion, during which media representatives were briefed about the activities undertaken as part of the Ayurveda Day celebrations and their objectives.

The activities organised at CARI on the occasion of the 11th Ayurveda Day highlighted the importance of Ayurveda, healthy lifestyles and preventive healthcare, while promoting greater public awareness about the traditional system of medicine.

2314168.title: Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman inaugurates BRICS Heads of Tax Authorities Meeting in New Delhi
2314168.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman inaugurates BRICS Heads of Tax Authorities Meeting in New Delhi
India’s BRICS Tax Chairship delivers landmark outcomes across technology, administration and people
Two new India-led Working Groups on International Taxation and Revenue Statistics formally established; BRICS Tax Progress Report 2026 adopted
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 8:38PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman inaugurated the BRICS Heads of Tax Authorities Meeting in New Delhi today, as the culmination of India’s BRICS Chairship of the tax cooperation track. The meeting was also addressed by the Union Finance Minister, Union Minister of State for Finance Shri Pankaj Chaudhary, and Revenue Secretary Shri Arvind Shrivastava.

The meeting was attended by Shri Ravi Agrawal, Chairman, CBDT, Shri Prasenjit Singh, Member (Legislation), CBDT, other Members of CBDT, and senior officers of the Department of Revenue (DoR). The meeting, hosted by the Central Board of Direct Taxes, Ministry of Finance, Government of India, brought together the Heads of Tax Authorities of the BRICS member countries. Representatives from ten BRICS tax administrations - Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, South Africa, and the United Arab Emirates - came together at one place to share their experiences and discuss emerging challenges through cooperation and collaboration.

In her address on the occasion, Smt. Sitharaman highlighted technology, administration and people as the three recurring themes of BRICS tax cooperation during India’s Chairship. She emphasised the role of data and digital infrastructure in making tax administration more precise and accessible, the importance of durable institutional mechanisms and practical tools that can sustain cooperation beyond individual Chairships, and the value of investing in people and building professional relationships across tax administrations. She also underscored that the perspectives of BRICS economies are essential to ensuring the fairness and durability of ongoing multilateral tax negotiations, including the negotiations on the UN Framework Convention on International Tax Cooperation.

The meeting formally adopted several landmark outcomes. Two new Working Groups on International Taxation and Transfer Pricing, and on Revenue Statistics, were established. Both will be led by India, creating sustained institutional platforms that will continue regardless of the Chairship. The first-ever in-person BRICS Young Tax Professionals Capacity Building Programme, held at the National Academy of Direct Taxes, Nagpur in April 2026, was institutionalised as an annual feature of BRICS tax cooperation. The BRICS Tax Cross-Learning Lab was formally launched, integrating the work of the Client-Centric Administration and HR Practices Working Groups into a joint peer-learning platform. The Terms of Reference of the BRICS Tax Support Network was also approved.

The meeting concluded with the formal signing of the BRICS Tax Progress Report 2026, the complete record of India’s Chairship of the BRICS Tax track. The People’s Republic of China was welcomed as the incoming Chair of the BRICS tax cooperation track for 2027.

The Heads of Tax Authorities lauded the Government of India for the successful organisation of the meeting and for the quality and depth of India’s Chairship of the BRICS tax track.

2314163.title: ELDERLINE 14567 Provides Information, Guidance and Support to Senior Citizens Across India; Launched On 1st October 2021
2314163.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
ELDERLINE 14567 Provides Information, Guidance and Support to Senior Citizens Across India; Launched On 1st October 2021
Over 29 lakh calls received including 8.67 Lakh Actionable Calls (Covered Information, Guidance, Emotional Support, Field Intervention) Since FY 2021–September 2026
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 8:36PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is providing senior citizens with access to information, guidance, emotional support and assistance through ELDERLINE 14567, the National Helpline for Senior Citizens (NHSC). The toll-free helpline is a component of the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY).

Joint Secretary Senior Citizen Division in the Ministry Shri Sajeesh Kumar N said that ELDERLINE is operational in 32 States and Union Territories. He said over 29 Lakh calls have been received on the HELPLINE. He further said the National Institute of Social Defence (NISD), which monitors its implementation, has catered to more than 8.67 Lakh Actionable Calls covering information, guidance, emotional support and field intervention  since FY 2021 upto September 21, 2026 which remains a continuous process.

The Joint Secretary said the ELDERLINE connects callers with assistance suited to their needs whileas the State Connect Centres provide information and guidance, offer emotional support and counselling and coordinate field interventions wherever required.

He added that depending on the nature of a grievance, they work with State Social Welfare Departments, police, healthcare institutions, legal aid services, senior citizen homes and other local agencies and the State Governments facilitate intervention and rehabilitation at the field level wherever necessary.

Joint Secretary said the Ministry implements the HELPLINE through agreements with participating State and Union Territory governments and service providers.

Shri Sajeesh Kumar N further said that NISD and the respective governments monitor calls, services, grievances and field interventions through periodic progress reports.

He further said that the Ministry also reviews digital service delivery, awareness activities, outreach, accessibility and coordination with local authorities to improve support for senior citizens, including those in remote areas.

It is pertinent to mention that Senior Citizens seeking assistance can call the TOLL-FREE ELDERLINE NUMBER 14567. The helpline coordinates services and referrals; it does not provide direct financial assistance to callers.

2314150.title: DRI seizes 86 live Tokay Geckos in Assam in a crackdown on wildlife trafficking; two arrested
2314150.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
DRI seizes 86 live Tokay Geckos in Assam in a crackdown on wildlife trafficking; two arrested
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 8:13PM by PIB Delhi

Acting on specific intelligence regarding an illegal wildlife trade deal, officers of DRI, intercepted two persons at Bandar Chalia Gaon Ground, Mariani, Assam, on 22.09.2026.


During the operation, 86 live Tokay Geckos, an endangered wildlife species, were recovered from their possession and seized under the provisions of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

The Tokay Gecko is listed under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and under Appendix-II of CITES, regulating its international trade. The two apprehended persons, along with the recovered live geckos, were subsequently handed over to the, Mariani Range Forest office, Assam, for further action under the relevant provisions of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

The operation highlights DRI’s continued efforts to detect and disrupt illegal trafficking of wildlife species, including those targeted for their perceived medicinal properties and demand as exotic pets in illicit markets.

2314148.title: DRI seizes 10,000 kg of firecrackers worth Rs. 3 crore at Nhava Sheva port
2314148.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
DRI seizes 10,000 kg of firecrackers worth Rs. 3 crore at Nhava Sheva port
Firecrackers concealed behind declared cargo of bottles; key syndicate member arrested
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 8:07PM by PIB Delhi

In an intelligence led operation, officers of DRI, intercepted an import consignment at Nhava Sheva Port suspected to contain firecrackers and on examination of the same found firecrackers concealed under the guise of declared goods, namely “Bottle & Wallpaper.”

 

 

 

Seized firecracker 288 Gatling


The detailed examination led to recovery of 19,800 pieces of firecrackers (known as 288 Gatling), weighing approximately 10,000 Kg with a market value of about Rs. 3 crore. Except for the first three rows containing the declared goods, the container was found to be filled predominantly with firecrackers. The firecrackers, along with the declared cover cargo, were seized under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.

The import of firecrackers is 'Restricted' under the Foreign Trade Policy and requires valid authorisation from DGFT, and requisite license from the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organization (PESO) under the Explosives Rules, 2008.

During the course of investigation, the key syndicate member, who was orchestrating and attempting the clandestine clearance of the said goods, has been arrested under the Customs Act, 1962.

The operation underscores DRI’s continued focus on detecting misdeclaration and clandestine import of restricted goods through commercial cargo channels.
