2313647.body_html:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
President of India Smt. Droupadi Murmu Confers 72nd National Film Awards at Ekta Nagar, Gujarat
The President urges the film fraternity to promote a healthy lifestyle and avoid endorsing harmful substances, as they are role models for the youth.
Dadasaheb Phalke Award Winner Anant Nag Expresses Gratitude for the immense love he has received from the countless people of the nation
National Film Awards to showcase India's Cultural Diversity by Taking Ceremony to Key Tourist Destinations: Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw
I&B Minister Announces next edition of WAVES to be Held in October 2027
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 8:34PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, today conferred the 72nd National Film Awards and congratulated all the award winners for their talent, dedication and hard work. She said filmmaking is a collaborative effort and urged the awardees to convey her appreciation to every member of their teams whose contributions made the award-winning films possible.

The President congratulated Dadasaheb Phalke Award recipient Shri Anant Nag for his distinguished contribution to theatre and cinema.

Veteran actor Anant Nag receives the #DadasahebPhalkeAward at the 72nd National Film Awards, recognising his remarkable contribution to Indian cinema. 🎬🏆👏#IndiaCelebratesCinema #FilmsThatUnite pic.twitter.com/4MDY4LNqcP

— PIB India (@PIB_India) September 22, 2026

The President said Indian cinema reflects the country’s diverse languages, traditions, aspirations and struggles. She appreciated the choice of Ekta Nagar as venue of the National Film Awards, symbolising India’s cultural and national unity.

Calling for dignity and social security in the creative economy, the President said workers, small artists, assistants and struggling members of the creative community deserve respect and social security. She also called for women’s participation in all jury to ensure a comprehensive human perspective.

 

Highlighting the influence of popular artists, particularly on children and young people, the President urged successful artists to promote the benefits of a disciplined lifestyle and refrain from endorsing substances harmful to health.

The President said the quality of films being made in the country strengthens her belief that Indian cinema can set world-class standards.

A Lifetime of Stories, A Legacy of Cinema: Shri Anant Nag Honoured with Dadasaheb Phalke Award 

As the President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, presented the prestigious Dadasaheb Phalke Award 2024 to Shri Anant Nag, the moment celebrated his lifetime of dedication to storytelling, theatre and cinema. The honour recognised his memorable performances and enduring contribution to Indian cinema over the decades.

Accepting the award with humility, Shri Anant Nag expressed gratitude for the people and experiences that shaped his journey.

 

Recalling his early years, Shri Anant Nag said that he grew up in an ashram before being sent to Mumbai, where he got an opportunity to act in a play. Theatre became the foundation of his career, and he went on to perform in around 50 plays before entering films. He later had the opportunity to work in films, including those made by acclaimed filmmaker Shyam Benegal.

Shri Anant Nag said he consciously chose Kannada cinema and made Bengaluru his karmabhoomi. Recalling that he was honoured with the Padma Bhushan by the Hon’ble President last year, he expressed his deep gratitude for receiving the Dadasaheb Phalke Award from the President once again this year.

 

Gujarat Welcomes the National Film Awards

The ceremony in Gujarat marked a new chapter in the journey of the National Film Awards.

The Governor of Gujarat Acharya Devvrat expressed gratitude to the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting for beginning the tradition of holding the National Film Awards outside Delhi, and said it was a matter of pride for Gujarat to host the prestigious awards at Ekta Nagar, Kevadia, associated with the legacy and strength of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

Addressing the 72nd National Film Awards ceremony, the Governor said Indian cinema has contributed significantly to enriching the country’s diverse languages and cultures.

He urged filmmakers to use cinema to promote natural farming, healthy lifestyles and environmental consciousness, and to strengthen values of love, brotherhood and national unity.

Gujarat Chief Minister Shri Bhupendra PateI welcomed the Hon’ble President and distinguished guests to Gujarat for the 72nd National Film Awards, describing the hosting of the ceremony at Ekta Nagar as a matter of pride for the State.

He highlighted cinema as a reflection of society, a carrier of culture and a powerful medium for connecting human emotions, with the potential to strengthen India’s global identity and soft power.

Highlighting Gujarat’s rich heritage, diverse landscapes and cultural traditions, he invited Indian and international filmmakers to choose Gujarat for filming and thanked the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting for bringing the prestigious ceremony to the State.

 

Union Minister for Information & Broadcasting Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw expressed gratitude to the Hon’ble President for gracing the 72nd National Film Awards ceremony at Ekta Nagar, Kevadia, and congratulated all the award winners for their outstanding achievements in Indian cinema.

The Minister said that cinema is a team effort and that the National Film Awards recognise both those receiving awards and those working behind the scenes. He also lauded Dadasaheb Phalke Award recipient Shri Anant Nag for his immense contribution to Indian cinema.

 

Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw said that the focus of the National Film Awards is to take the ceremony to important tourist destinations across States and Union Territories, thereby promoting India’s rich cultural heritage and tourism. He called upon the states & union territories to pitch for tourist destinations as venues for the future editions of national film awards.

Highlighting the Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT) as a new talent pool, he said that around 380 students have already enrolled in 13 courses, with the curriculum designed and driven by the industry. He further informed that the Hon’ble Prime Minister has approved 15,000 Creative Labs across the country, creating new opportunities for youth to learn emerging technologies and showcase India’s diverse culture.

The Minister called upon filmmakers and the entire film fraternity, with Shri Prasoon Joshi as Chairman of Prasar Bharati, to help identify, nurture and promote raw talent from small towns.

He reiterated that combined efforts of the Government and the creative fraternity can help unlock India’s immense creative potential and enable Indian talent to reach audiences across the world.

He also invited suggestions and ideas for WAVES 2027, to be held in October next year.

 

The Secretary, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Shri Chanchal Kumar, said that at the 72nd National Film Awards, 400 Feature Films across 34 languages and 161 Non-Feature Films across 24 languages were received, with 22 Feature Film and 23 Non-Feature Film awards conferred. He said that Indian cinema continues to grow as a powerful medium of cultural expression and global storytelling.

The Secretary said that holding the National Film Awards outside Delhi, at Ekta Nagar, is an important initiative inspired by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's vision and commitment to national unity, and that in the coming years, the ceremony is also envisaged to be held in other cities.

Celebrating Excellence: Stories, Performances and the Many Shades of Indian Cinema

The best actor in a Leading Role award was shared Mammootty for Bramayugam  & Kartik Aaryan for Chandu Champion, while Yami Gautam received the Best Actress in a Leading Role award for Article 370.

In the supporting categories, Sanjay Mishra was honoured as Best Actor in a Supporting Role for Bhakshak, while Sachana Namidass for Maharaja and Ropashree Varkady for Mithya shared the Best Actress in a Supporting Role award.

Article 370 was honoured as the Best Feature Film, while Randeep Hooda received recognition for his directorial debut, Swatantrya Veer Savarkar. Kalki 2898 AD was named Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment, while Captain Miller received the award for Best Feature Film Promoting National, Social and Environmental Values. Rajkumar Periasamy received the Best Direction award for Amaran.

Many Languages, One National Stage

The awards also highlighted the linguistic diversity of Indian cinema. Beyond the languages specified in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, Garhwali and Tulu cinema too found national recognition.

Dholi, produced by SC Pharmachem Pvt. Ltd. and directed by Dinesh P. Bhonsle, received the Best Garhwali Film award, while IMBU, produced by Pichchar Studio and directed by Shivadhwaj Shetty, was honoured as the Best Tulu Film.

Angen, a Santhali film directed by Ravi Raj Murmu, received the Best Debut Film of a Director award.

From Garhwali and Tulu to Santhali, the evening brought diverse cinematic voices to one national platform reaffirming that every language adds a new story to India’s cinematic tapestry.

 

A Celebration of Indian Cinema

The 72nd National Film Awards brought together celebrated names, emerging voices, popular cinema and regional storytelling on one national stage. At Ekta Nagar, the evening became a celebration of India’s cinematic spirit many languages, countless stories and diverse creative traditions coming together through the universal language of cinema.

For the complete list of award recipients and detailed information on the awards, please click : Complete List of Awardees

******

2313640.title: NHRC, India holds Statutory Full Commission Meeting in New Delhi
2313640.body_html:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India holds Statutory Full Commission Meeting in New Delhi
The meeting aimed to enhance synergy and cooperation among the Commissions for the promotion and protection of human rights
Chairing the meeting, Chairperson Justice V. Ramasubramanian says, the NHRC may explore extending support to other Commissions if lacking in machinery in the investigation of cases
Shares concerns over the lack of rehabilitation of mentally ill women engaged in begging, social security for PwDs and the denial of insurance coverage to them by insurance companies
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 8:20PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India, organised a Statutory Full Commission meeting with representatives of all seven deemed members of the Commission in New Delhi today. The meeting aimed to enhance synergy and cooperation among the Commissions for the promotion and protection of human rights.

Chairing the meeting, Justice Shri V. Ramasubramanian, Chairperson, NHRC, India, emphasised the importance of collaborative functioning among the Commissions. He said that the Chairpersons of all the National Commissions are ex-officio Members of the NHRC and, therefore, are part of it. He said that together, the Commissions can undertake meaningful work for promoting and protecting the human rights of various sections of society.

Justice Ramasubramanian suggested appointing a Nodal Officer to coordinate among all the National Commissions. He said that the NHRC may explore extending support to other Commissions if lacking in machinery in the investigation of cases. In his concluding remarks, he also shared the concern over the lack of rehabilitation measures for mentally ill women engaged in begging, which requires attention. He noted that there is a sizeable population of persons with disabilities (PwDs) worldwide and stressed the need to examine policies intended for their welfare and identify gaps. The NHRC, India Chairperson expressed concern over the lack of social security for PwDs and the denial of insurance coverage by insurance companies. He also appreciated the suggestion for interfaith dialogue and coordinated research, particularly in overlapping areas.

The meeting discussed issues including an integrated approach towards protecting the rights of vulnerable and marginalised sections, identification of key areas for collaborative efforts, sharing of best practices and minimising duplication of cases. The participants emphasised the need for joint fact-finding efforts, research, awareness campaigns and outreach programmes.

Smt. Vijaya K. Rahatkar, Chairperson, National Commission for Women (NCW), highlighted the work of the NCW towards promoting and protecting women's rights and various programmes, including public hearings organised in different districts to hear their complaints. She said that, besides handling complaints, the NCW also focuses on research, awareness and outreach training programmes for the welfare of women. She added that the NCW has been organising anti-human trafficking campaigns in collaboration with Central Armed Police Forces and holding dialogues with youth on POSH, POCSO and cybercrime-related issues in collaboration with different institutions.

Smt. Kiran Umesh Mahalle, Member, National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC), spoke about the problems faced by the beggar community, particularly those suffering from mental health issues. She expressed concern over mentally ill women being left by their families to beg on the roads. She suggested that the National Commissions may consider formulating a policy for their rehabilitation and recommending its implementation to the Government.

Shri S. Govindraj, Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities (CCPD) said that the CCPD has been focusing on reaching those who have remained unreached. He stressed the need for research into gaps in welfare measures for persons with disabilities, who he described as among the most vulnerable populations facing discrimination.

Dr. Sanjeev Sharma, Member Secretary, National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR), highlighted the NCPCR's work on rescue and rehabilitation of children in a campaign mode. He said that over 8,000 children have been rescued and rehabilitated. He also underscored the need for capacity building and training. He said that the circulation of child sexual abuse material on social media platforms requires immediate attention. He suggested joint investigations and joint bench sittings of Statutory Commission members, besides strengthening State Commissions.

Shri Vivek Kumar Dewangan, Secretary, National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC), said that the NCSC has set up an e-grievance monitoring portal, which has resulted in quicker redressal of grievances. He emphasised better coordination among the Statutory Commission members, collaboration on capacity building and awareness in educational institutions, joint studies on socio-economic indicators and joint action plans with measurable objectives.

Shri Suchindra Misra, Secretary, National Commission for Minorities (NCM), highlighted the importance of electronic grievance redressal systems and capacity building with support from the NHRC. He also stressed coordination with States to establish State Minority Commissions, noting that only 18 States have such Commissions so far. He further underscored the significance of coordinated research and complaint redressal, besides holding interfaith dialogues.

Shri Manohar N. Sukole, Deputy Secretary, National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST), highlighting the importance of registering of suomotu cases besides the need for establishing grievance redressal platforms with real time tracking provisions and early warning systems identifying the recurring issues and overlapping matters requiring a more integrated approach among Statutory Commission Members.

Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi, Member, NHRC, India said that the endeavour should be to work together to ensure that benefits reach the grassroots level. He said that while the Statutory Commission members work in different fields, their purpose is the same. He observed that SOPs can be effective if implemented properly and emphasised the need for adequate staff and infrastructure for all the Commissions to achieve their objectives.

Dr. Anupama Nilekar Chandra, DG (Inv) NHRC, India said that the Commission will be organising a training programme for investigation officers on the last Wednesday of each month beginning 30th September 2026. It will be further expanded over the course of time.

Earlier, setting the agenda for the meeting, Shri Piyush Goyal, Secretary General, NHRC, India, gave an overview of the country's unique institutional human rights protection framework. He emphasised that interactions among these institutions are useful in forming synergy and cooperation between different Commissions to protect the rights of vulnerable and disadvantaged communities including bonded labours, older persons and manual scavengers. The interactions can also help in paving the way forward for capacity building and sharing of best practices.

Shri Samir Kumar, Joint Secretary, NHRC, India, summarised the activities undertaken by the Commission over the last year.

The meeting concluded with a renewed commitment to collaborative efforts among the Commissions for the promotion and protection of human rights in India.

2313633.title: MCL Targets 10 Lakh Sq. Ft. Clean-Up under Special Campaign 6.0
2313633.body_html:
Ministry of Coal
MCL Targets 10 Lakh Sq. Ft. Clean-Up under Special Campaign 6.0
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 8:02PM by PIB Delhi

Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL) has stepped up preparations for Special Campaign 6.0, with an ambitious target to clean more than 10 lakh square feet of area across its offices, colonies and other establishments during the campaign period.

The target marks a significant step-up from the previous campaign, during which MCL covered 6.12 lakh square feet of identified areas, reflecting the company’s continued efforts towards creating cleaner, more organised and efficient workplaces.

The campaign is being undertaken in line with the Government of India’s Special Campaign 6.0, scheduled from October 2 to October 31, 2026 focused on institutionalising Swachhata, improving workplace management, optimising available space, reducing pendency and ensuring effective collection, segregation and disposal of waste, including e-waste.

The key focus area of this year’s campaign will be the scientific management of e-waste generated across MCL offices and establishments.

Dedicated efforts will be undertaken for the identification, segregation and systematic disposal of obsolete and discarded electronic items in accordance with applicable guidelines. The initiative is aimed at strengthening responsible waste management practices while simultaneously helping offices create cleaner, safer and more organised workspaces.

The campaign will place especial emphasis on space optimisation, enabling better utilisation of workplace areas by identifying and clearing unwanted, obsolete and redundant materials.

Through Special Campaign 6.0, MCL aims to further strengthen a culture of cleanliness, environmental responsibility and efficient workplace management across its Offices and establishments.

2313630.title: Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy Holds Talks with European Parliament’s ITRE Delegation.
2313630.body_html:
Ministry of Heavy Industries
Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy Holds Talks with European Parliament’s ITRE Delegation.
Highlights India-EU cooperation in EVs, batteries, industrial decarbonisation and green steel.
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 7:52PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel Shri H.D. Kumaraswamy today held discussions with a delegation of the Committee on Industry, Research and Energy (ITRE) of the European Parliament in New Delhi on strengthening India-EU cooperation in industrial development, clean energy, electric mobility and industrial decarbonisation. The European Parliament delegation comprised Members of the European Parliament Mr Raffaele Stancanelli, Ms Angelika Winzig, Mr Mohammed Chahim, Mr Raúl de la Hoz Quintano, Mr Nicolas Gonzalez Casares, Mr Morten Løkke­gaard, Mr Jüri Ratas and Mr Virginijus Sinkevičius. The delegation was accompanied by Mr Etienne Bassot, Director, ITRE Secretariat; Mr Mariusz Kawnik, Administrator, ITRE Secretariat; Mr Brahim Ebn Aissa, Assistant, ITRE Secretariat; and other staff.

The Minister said the visit comes at an important juncture in India-EU relations, following the 16th India-EU Summit in January 2026, which witnessed the conclusion of the FTA negotiations and adoption of the Joint India-EU Comprehensive Strategic Agenda. He emphasised the potential for deeper cooperation in trade, investment, technology and global supply chains.

Shri Kumaraswamy highlighted key initiatives of the Ministry of Heavy Industries, including the PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Components, PLI Scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cells and PM E-DRIVE, aimed at promoting domestic manufacturing, accelerating electric mobility and strengthening the EV ecosystem. He also invited European industries to participate in the ongoing global bidding process for 10 GWh of ACC manufacturing for stationary storage energy systems, open until October 13, 2026.

The Minister highlighted India’s efforts towards industrial decarbonisation and energy transition, including BHEL’s indigenous gasification technology and the roadmap for greening the steel sector through scrap recycling, utilisation of steel slag and circular economy practices.

Senior officials from the Ministry of Heavy Industries and Steel, including Secretary Shri Kamran Rizvi and Additional Secretary Shri Hanif Qureshi, also participated in the meeting.

The delegation appreciated India’s efforts towards accelerating electric mobility, strengthening domestic manufacturing and advancing industrial decarbonisation. The members also expressed interest in further strengthening India-EU cooperation in clean technologies, sustainable mobility and advanced energy solutions.

Shri Kumaraswamy said India and the EU can combine their strengths to accelerate the clean energy transition and advance sustainable transport through innovative e-mobility solutions. He expressed confidence in continued engagement and deeper cooperation in the industrial sector.

2313612.title: Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu launches Challenge Mode for Aerodrome Development
2313612.body_html:
Ministry of Civil Aviation
Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu launches Challenge Mode for Aerodrome Development
Next Phase of UDAN Takes Off with MoUs Signed with 21 States/UTs
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 7:10PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Civil Aviation today took a major step towards strengthening regional air connectivity across the country with the signing of 21 Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with States and Union Territories under the next phase of the UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik) Scheme. The MoUs mark a significant milestone in Centre–State/UT cooperation for the development of aviation infrastructure and expansion of air connectivity to underserved and unserved regions.

The ceremony, held at The Ashok, Chanakyapuri, New Delhi, was inaugurated by Shri Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu, Minister of Civil Aviation, in the presence of Shri Murlidhar Mohol, Minister of State for Civil Aviation; Shri Samir Kumar Sinha, Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation; Shri Vipin Kumar, Chairman, Airports Authority of India (AAI), and senior officials of the Ministry.

"With these MoUs, Team Bharat is joining hands to take India's regional aviation to greater heights. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Viksit Rajya is the foundation of Viksit Bharat, with every State as an equal partner in this journey," said Shri Ram Mohan Naidu Kinjarapu.

Talking about the impact of UDAN, the Minister added, "Since its launch, UDAN has operationalized 687 routes and 95 aerodromes, with more than 3.66 lakh flights carrying around 1.71 crore passengers. But the numbers that matter most to me are the numbers of impact, aviation-sector jobs have grown from around 3 million in 2014 to nearly 7.7 million today, with the potential to reach 25 million by 2040. Airports like Tezu in Arunachal Pradesh and Purnea in Bihar, once cut off from air connectivity by hundreds of kilometers, are today becoming drivers of regional prosperity”.

The launch of the next phase of UDAN builds on the inauguration by the Prime Minister at Jodhpur on 4th July 2026 and the UDAN Workshop held on 16th July 2026, which brought together civil aviation stakeholders to deliberate on the roadmap for the next phase of the scheme.

"Modified UDAN rests on four pillars; affordability for passengers, sustainability of operations, transparent Challenge Mode framework for projects and the promotion of indigenous manufacturing. Together, we are building an ecosystem towards the larger ambition of Made in India Civil aircraft. That is the direction in which this next phase of UDAN is taking us", Shri Ram Mohan Naidu added.

With today’s launch, the next phase of UDAN moves from policy and stakeholder consultations towards on-ground implementation, with a three-pronged focus on strengthening Centre–State/UT partnerships, creating aviation infrastructure and expanding regional air connectivity.

Speaking at the event, Minister of State for Civil Aviation Shri Murlidhar Mohol said, “Under the able leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, UDAN has come a long way since 2016 expanding regional and remote connectivity across the country. Now, with Modified UDAN, we are looking at 120 new destinations and 4 crore more passengers over the next ten years. With more than 20 States coming together, we are taking this journey forward and opening a new chapter in India’s civil aviation sector.”

A total of 21 MoUs were signed between the Ministry of Civil Aviation, participating States/UTs and the Airports Authority of India (AAI), the implementing agency under the UDAN Scheme. The MoUs establish a structured framework for coordinated action between the Centre, States/UTs and AAI for identification, development and operationalisation of aviation assets, aligned with the connectivity requirements and priorities of States and UTs.

The Civil Aviaation Minister also launched the Challenge Mode Portal for Aerodrome Development and released the Scheme Document for the next phase of UDAN Route Bidding.

Under the Challenge Mode, State Governments and UT Administrations will now be able to nominate airstrips and helipads for development under the next phase of UDAN through the dedicated portal. This will enable States/UTs to proactively identify locations with potential for aviation connectivity and facilitate the creation and upgradation of aviation infrastructure based on local requirements.

The route bidding round will invite airlines to bid for identified UDAN routes, enabling transparent and competitive selection of routes and operators. The process will facilitate the expansion of air services to unserved and underserved regions, improving accessibility and mobility and supporting wider economic activity, tourism, trade and employment.

The event also featured a technical session on the next phase of UDAN, covering the Challenge Mode for aerodrome development and the upcoming bidding round for selection of UDAN routes. The session provided an opportunity for States/UTs, AAI, airlines and other civil aviation stakeholders to deliberate on the implementation framework and way forward.

The next phase of UDAN seeks to build on the gains achieved under the scheme and further deepen the aviation ecosystem across the country, ensuring that the benefits of air connectivity and aviation infrastructure reach more regions, communities and citizens.

2313605.title: 11th Ayurveda Day to be Celebrated Across India and Worldwide on 23 September
2313605.body_html:
AYUSH
11th Ayurveda Day to be Celebrated Across India and Worldwide on 23 September
Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow: Focus on Evidence, Research, Innovation and Community Wellbeing
Ayurveda Day to Witness Launch of Safety Dossiers, Guidelines, Reports and CCRAS–AGNI Web Portal
First-Ever Report on Ayush Services Sector to be Launched on Ayurveda Day
Scientific Sessions to Deliberate on Ayurveda's Road to 2047 and Reducing NCD Burden
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 6:55PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Ayush will host the 11th Ayurveda Day celebrations tomorrow in Nagpur under the theme “Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow (स्वस्थ भविष्य के लिए आयुर्वेद)”. Ayurveda institutions, practitioners and stakeholders will participate in the celebrations across India and worldwide.

The national programme at Nagpur will witness the launch of the first-ever Report on the “Ayush Services Sector”, prepared by the Research and Information System for Developing Countries (RIS), providing an assessment of the Ayush services sector. The programme will also feature the launch of Safety Dossiers on Gokshura (Tribulus terrestris) and Chandrasura (Lepidium sativum), Standard Treatment Guidelines (STGs) on Skin Disorders, and other initiatives and publications aimed at strengthening evidence, research, innovation and community wellbeing in Ayurveda.

The programme will also witness the launch of “From Traditional Wisdom to Global Leadership: Ayush Vision 2030” Report, the Status Report on Ayush-related Inventions in India, and the CCRAS–AGNI (Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences – Ayurveda Gyan Naipunya Initiative) Assessment Scale Web Portal.

The event will feature two scientific sessions. Scientific Session I, titled “Shashwatam to Vishwas - Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow and the Road to 2047”, and Scientific Session II, titled “Integrating Therapies is needed to reduce NCD (Non-Communicable Diseases) Burden by 2027”.

Senior officials of the Ministry of Ayush, representatives of the Councils and various Ayush institutions will be present at the event. The celebrations will bring together key stakeholders from across the Ayurveda ecosystem, providing a platform for knowledge exchange and wider engagement.

The 11th Ayurveda Day celebrations will highlight the importance of evidence, research and innovation in strengthening Ayurveda and advancing community wellbeing. The nationwide and worldwide observance will reinforce the focus on Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow.

2313599.body_html:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
Vice-President Inaugurates 9th India International Water Week 2026
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Calls for Collective Action and Innovation to Build a Water-Secure and Climate-Resilient India
Union Jal Shakti Minister Shri C R Patil Emphasises Cooperation and Jan Bhagidari for Water Security
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 6:27PM by PIB Delhi

The Hon’ble Vice-President of India Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurated the 9th India International Water Week (IIWW) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, today in the presence of Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C R Patil, Ministers of State for Jal Shakti Shri V. Somanna and Shri Raj Bhushan Choudhary. Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation Smt. Archana Verma, and Chairman, Central Water Commission Shri Anupam Prasad and representatives from India and abroad, Ambassadors, global water leaders, senior officials, representatives of international organisations, experts, researchers, industry, innovators and other stakeholders were also present.

Organised by the Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India, from 22 to 26 September 2026, the five-day event is being held on the theme “Climate Resilient Water Management.” The ninth edition marks an important milestone as the event, organised in its earlier editions as India Water Week, has evolved into India International Water Week, reflecting its growing global engagement and the increasing importance of international cooperation in addressing shared water challenges.

The Netherlands and Germany are participating as partner Countries, along with 14 States as partner States and two Central Ministries as partner Ministries. The event brings together governments, international and multilateral organisations, research and academic institutions, industry, civil society, start-ups, innovators and young professionals. It provides a comprehensive platform for policy dialogue, technology demonstration, knowledge exchange, networking, business tie-ups and new collaborations.

Addressing the inaugural session, the Vice-President emphasised the growing challenges to water security posed by climate change, urbanisation and increasing pressure on natural resources. He called for integrated and sustainable management of water through innovation, efficiency and collective action. He underscored the critical role of interlinking of rivers in addressing spatial and temporal variations in water availability. He appreciated the various interventions undertaken by the Ministry of Jal Shakti and applauded the achievements made. Recalling his tenure as Governor of Jharkhand, the Vice-President noted that rural tap water coverage in the State rose from about 7% to 37% under Jal Jeevan Mission. He described the Mission as a transformative programme that has significantly expanded access to potable drinking water in rural households.

He also highlighted the significance of cooperative arrangements among States for sharing and management of inter-state river waters. He called upon the participants to use IIWW 2026 to exchange knowledge, strengthen partnerships and translate deliberations into concrete action. He also launched two important publications, namely, “Sustainable Urban River Management Framework” and “AI and ML Driven Integrated Reservoir Sediment Management.”

Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C R Patil, said that water security and climate resilience must go hand in hand, as many of the impacts of climate change are increasingly being experienced through water. He highlighted India’s Water Vision@2047 and major interventions including Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana, Jal Jeevan Mission, Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari, Namami Gange, Atal Bhujal Yojana, NAQUIM, the Ken-Betwa Link Project, Dam Rehabilitation and Improvement Project and the National Hydrology Project. The minister added that Jan Bhagidari is our biggest strength where we learn from each other and share experiences to advance water management. He underlined the transformative potential of research and development, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, remote sensing, GIS, real-time sensors and advanced modelling, while stressing that technology must work together with strong institutions, local knowledge and community participation.

Welcoming the participants, Smt. Archana Verma, Secretary, Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, said that IIWW has evolved into an important multidisciplinary global platform for dialogue, knowledge sharing, technology demonstration and partnerships. She stressed that climate resilience needs to be integrated into the planning, financing, development, operation and management of water resources and infrastructure. She expressed confidence that the deliberations would lead to actionable recommendations, scalable solutions, exchange of best practices and stronger partnerships.

The inaugural session also recognised the contribution of grassroots Water Warriors. Mrs. Ram Kumari from Chhindwara, Madhya Pradesh was recognised for mobilising women and communities around drinking water availability and water conservation, including efforts that helped improve drinking water access for around 225 families. Shri Sitaram Madavi of Gadchiroli, Maharashtra, who has worked for over two decades on water conservation, rural development and agricultural sustainability, was recognised for developing wells, farm ponds and other water conservation interventions that have contributed to improved groundwater availability and irrigation access.

Following the inaugural session, a high-level Ministerial Plenary on “Country Perspectives on Climate Resilient Water Management” brought together perspectives from India and international partners. The session focused on the need to move beyond reactive water management towards systems capable of anticipating risks, adapting to change and recovering from climate extremes. Discussions covered climate-informed infrastructure, flood and drought management, digital hydrology and early warning, nature-based solutions, water-use efficiency, institutional capacity and international cooperation.

Opening the Ministerial Plenary, Shri C R Patil highlighted India’s cooperation with countries including Venezuela, the Netherlands and Denmark. He also emphasised the important role of multilateral and international institutions such as the World Bank and IUCN. He called for deeper collaboration in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, information technology, remote sensing, joint research, capacity building and demonstration projects, stressing the need to move from exchanging knowledge to creating knowledge together and from responding to water crises to building resilience before crises occur.

Addressing the Ministerial Plenary, Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation Shri Ashok K.K. Meena said that under the Jal Jeevan Mission, we have learnt that resilience is not merely about creating infrastructure; it is about ensuring reliable and sustainable water services over time, with communities playing a central role in planning, operation and long-term sustainability. The Secretary added that this must be supported by effective greywater management, groundwater recharge, and protection of water sources. Through the Decision Support System, he said that the department is enabling districts and Panchayats to identify vulnerable sources and prioritise such interventions. Every drop of water has a journey and every drop has value; Our collective responsibility is to ensure that this journey remains sustainable and the hydrological cycle remains unbroken for future generations.

Addressing the Plenary, the Vice Minister of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Venezuela, Ms. Yesenia Carolina Moreno Gerdel, emphasised the critical importance of protecting water sources, particularly during natural disasters such as earthquakes. She underscored that access to water is a fundamental human right and highlighted water as an essential source of life, peace and prosperity. Danish Ambassador to India H.E. Rasmus Abildgaard Kristensen, Ambassador of the Kingdom of the Netherlands to India Ms. Marisa Gerards, South Asia Regional Director World Bank Ms. Mara K. Warwick, Water Global Director IUCN Mr. James Dalton also participated in the Ministerial Plenary.

The Day One programme also included the inauguration of the international exhibition, which is being organised from 22 to 25 September. The exhibition provides a dedicated interface for governments, technology providers, research institutions, industries, start-ups and other stakeholders to showcase technologies, products and practical solutions for sustainable and climate-resilient water management.

Later in the day, the Global Water Leaders’ Plenary I on ‘Integrated Management of Water, Food & Energy’ highlighted the interdependence of water, food and energy systems and the importance of an integrated Water Food Energy nexus for climate-resilient development. The deliberations focused on water and resource security, irrigation efficiency and water productivity, micro-irrigation, solar-powered irrigation, digital monitoring, precision agriculture, data-driven decision making and stronger coordination among institutions.

The Global Water Leaders’ Plenary II on the Global River Cities Alliance focused on sustainable management of urban rivers and building climate-resilient river cities. The deliberations highlighted integrated policy frameworks, global knowledge exchange, Urban River Management Plans, technological and institutional innovations and opportunities for development agencies and public and private sector solution providers to cooperate on river-centric urban development. The session also included the launch of five Urban River Management Plans.

The Second International Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) Conference 2026, being organised concurrently with IIWW 2026, further strengthens the focus on drinking water, sanitation and hygiene in the context of climate change. The Conference brings together policymakers, practitioners, experts, development partners and other stakeholders to deliberate on climate-resilient WASH services, sustainability of drinking water sources, water quality, sanitation, wastewater management, technology and community participation. It provides an important platform for sharing experiences, innovations and scalable solutions towards achieving sustainable and resilient WASH services and advancing the objectives of SDG 6.

As part of the Conference, three thematic sessions were rganized covering key dimensions of climate-resilient WASH service delivery. The sessions focused on (i) Water Supply Systems: Operations & Maintenance, Infrastructure and Source Sustainability; (ii) Water Quality, Safety and Emerging Contaminants; and (iii) Climate Resilience, Nature-Based Solutions and Sanitation. The deliberations brought together policymakers, practitioners, researchers, development partners and sector experts to share their research papers for strengthening sustainable and resilient WASH systems.

Beyond formal deliberations, India International Water Week 2026 is designed as a platform for networking, institutional and business tie-ups, technology partnerships, joint research, knowledge exchange, capacity building and collaboration among governments, international organisations, academia, industry, start-ups and communities. Through its Ministerial and Global Water Leaders’ Plenaries, Country Forums, Water Leaders’ Forums, Practitioners’ Forums, Thematic Forums, Startup and Youth Forums, international exhibition and the concurrently organised Second International WASH Conference 2026, the event aims to translate dialogue into actionable recommendations, enduring partnerships and scalable solutions for a water-secure and climate-resilient future.

Day One concluded with Country Forum I on “Joint Indo-Danish Solutions for Sustainable Water Management.” The forum reflected the growing role of international cooperation in developing technology-enabled, efficiency-focused and data-driven water solutions. It explored opportunities in urban flooding and stormwater management, climate-induced extremes, digital decision-support systems, space technology, drones, robotics and advanced survey solutions. The broader objective was to facilitate cross-border partnerships, joint ventures, co-innovation, investment opportunities and stronger industry-academia-government linkages.

The discussions on the opening day conveyed a common message: climate-resilient water management requires integration across sectors, institutions and geographical boundaries; greater use of science, data and emerging technologies; strong institutions and community participation; and sustained international cooperation. IIWW 2026 seeks to take this agenda forward by connecting policy with practice, research with implementation and innovation with investment.

2313597.title: Assam’s Living Traditions and Cultural Legacy Features in PM Mementos e-Auction 2026
2313597.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
Assam’s Living Traditions and Cultural Legacy Features in PM Mementos e-Auction 2026
Assamese handlooms, bamboo and cane crafts, brassware and heritage artworks showcase the State’s distinctive cultural traditions
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 6:25PM by PIB Delhi

Assam’s rich cultural traditions and heritage find a distinctive representation in the 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026, with a collection of mementos showcasing the State’s renowned handloom traditions, bamboo and cane craftsmanship, metalwork, traditional art and heritage architecture.

The Assam collection brings together objects that reflect both the everyday craftsmanship and the deeper cultural memory of the State. Alongside traditional crafts and artworks, the collection features mementos associated with important historical personalities, cultural institutions and significant moments in Assam’s history.

These mementos offer a glimpse into the skills, traditions and cultural practices that have been passed down through generations and continue to form an important part of Assam’s cultural identity.

The collection also includes representations of Assam’s heritage and cultural institutions, bringing together material traditions with the State’s historical and spiritual legacy. Among the notable mementos are artworks and commemorative pieces associated with Bir Chilarai, Bharat Ratna awardee Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi, Swargadeo Chaolung Sukapha and Mahapurush Srimanta Sankardeva.

The collection also includes a representation of the 1894 Patharughat Battle, recalling an important chapter in Assam’s history, along with representations of Bordua Satra and Swahid Smarak Khetra & Park.

The Assam mementos form part of the larger collection of 1,498 mementos offered in the 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction.

The auction provides citizens, collectors, institutions, corporates and art and culture enthusiasts an opportunity to acquire mementos presented to the Prime Minister on various occasions. An accompanying exhibition at the National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA), New Delhi, enables visitors to view the mementos and appreciate their artistic and cultural significance.

The PM Mementos e-Auction is organised by the Ministry of Culture through the National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA), New Delhi. The funds raised through the auction are donated to the Namami Gange Programme, a national mission for the conservation and rejuvenation of the River Ganga.

The PM Mementos e-Auction 2026 is being conducted through the official portal: https://pmmementos.gov.in/#/

Among the standout contributions from Assam are:                                                                                    

Sati Sadhani Framed Muga Silk Artwork – An artwork depicting Sati Sadhani, the 16th-century Queen of the Chutia Kingdom, rendered in the traditional Ahom Kham style using golden-finished foils and organic colours on Muga silk.

Bamboo and Cane Wall Clock – A handcrafted clock made from natural bamboo and cane, reflecting Assam’s sustainable craftsmanship and traditional artistry.

Eco-Craft Gift Box – Artistry in Water Hyacinth – A collection of handwoven slippers, baskets, a natural-fibre hat and a painting, showcasing how water hyacinth is transformed into sustainable craft products and sources of livelihood for artisans.

Traditional Assamese Japi – Featuring vibrant red and blue patterns, the traditional Japi reflects Assam’s distinctive craft traditions and its longstanding association with hospitality, respect and honour.

Assamese Gamusa – Several traditional Gamusas feature in the collection, showcasing the State’s renowned handloom heritage through intricate red and gold motifs and traditional Assamese designs.

Assamese Brass Xorai – The collection includes several handcrafted brass Xorais, a traditional symbol of hospitality, respect and honour in Assamese culture, showcasing the State’s distinctive bell-metal craftsmanship.

Crafted Wooden Kamakhya Temple Replica – A finely crafted wooden miniature of the historic Kamakhya Temple, capturing its distinctive architectural form and traditional design elements.

2313577.title: Economic Inclusion Initiatives Promote Entrepreneurship, Livelihoods and Rehabilitation Among Marginalised Communities
2313577.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Economic Inclusion Initiatives Promote Entrepreneurship, Livelihoods and Rehabilitation Among Marginalised Communities
Over Rs 613 Crore Approved for 145 Companies under VCF-SC; Nearly Rs 143 Crore Approved for 31 Companies under VCF-BC
Investments Create Assets Worth Nearly Rs 800 Crore and Generate Around 4,500 Employment Opportunities
More than Rs 46 Crore Released for Comprehensive Rehabilitation of Persons Engaged in Begging
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 6:04PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, through its Economic Inclusion Division (EID), is strengthening entrepreneurship, livelihood generation and rehabilitation support for marginalised communities.

Its major initiatives include the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC), the Venture Capital Fund for Backward Classes and the comprehensive rehabilitation component for persons engaged in begging under the Support for Marginalised Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise Scheme.

Deputy Director General, Economic Inclusion Division (EID), in the Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment, Ms Pratima Gupta informed that under the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC) with a total corpus of Rs 750 crore, the Fund provides financial assistance ranging from Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 crore at an interest rate of 4 per cent.

She said from FY 2014-15 to FY 2025-26, the Fund has played an important role in enabling Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs to establish businesses, create productive assets and generate employment.

DDG EID further said that as of May 2026, the financial assistance of Rs 613.02 crore had been approved for 145 companies under the fund. Of this, Rs 437.74 crore had been disbursed to 123 companies, she added.

Ms Gupta said VCF-SC aims to promote entrepreneurship among members of Scheduled Caste communities by providing concessional financial assistance for establishing and expanding commercially viable enterprises.

The DDG EID said under VCF-SC, the Ministry launched the Ambedkar Social Innovation and Incubation Mission (ASIIM) on September 30, 2020 that supports innovative ideas developed by young Scheduled Caste researchers and students by providing financial assistance of up to Rs 30 lakh.

She added that under ASIIM, an amount of Rs 29.11 crore has been sanctioned to 114 companies, while Rs 13.27 crore has been disbursed to 91 companies wherein the Mission seeks to encourage technology-driven and socially relevant enterprises while developing an ecosystem of innovation among young entrepreneurs belonging to Scheduled Caste communities.

Talking about the Venture Capital Fund for Backward Classes (VCF-BC), the DDG EID said it was launched in October 2019 to promote entrepreneurship among individuals belonging to Backward Classes. With a corpus of Rs 200 crore, the fund provides financial assistance ranging from Rs 20 lakh to Rs 15 crore at an interest rate of 6 per cent, she further said.

Ms Gupta said financial assistance of Rs 142.88 crore has been approved for 31 companies, of which Rs 70.23 crore has been disbursed to 19 companies, as of now.

The DDG EID said Venture Capital Funds have supported 329 Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs and 35 entrepreneurs belonging to Backward Classes adding these investments have collectively generated around 4,500 direct and indirect employment opportunities.

She said the enterprises supported through these Funds have created permanent productive assets valued at nearly Rs 800 crores that are expected to contribute to economic activity, infrastructure development and employment generation over the next 12 to 15 years.

Ms Pratima further said as part of implementing the comprehensive rehabilitation component for persons engaged in begging under the Support for Marginalised Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise (SMILE) Scheme, the Ministry follows a comprehensive approach encompassing identification, mobilisation, rescue, shelter, counselling, healthcare, education, skill development, livelihood support and reintegration of persons engaged in begging.

The DDG EID said from the launch of the initiative on October 23, 2023 through FY 2025-26, the central assistance amounting to Rs 46.16 crore was released. Of this, an amount of Rs 27.17 crore was released during FY 2025-26 alone, she added.

Ms Pratima said through these initiatives, the Economic Inclusion Division is advancing the Government's commitment to social justice by enabling entrepreneurship, supporting enterprise creation, generating employment and facilitating the dignified rehabilitation and economic inclusion of marginalised communities.

2313570.title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah inaugurates 3rd National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) Heads of States/UTs in New Delhi
2313570.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah inaugurates 3rd National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) Heads of States/UTs in New Delhi
The roadmap of drug-free India is very important to achieve Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's goal of creating a Viksit Bharat by 2047
The time has come to take a strong and decisive blow on narcotics, which have become a serious threat to the country and the world
With the aim of improving the welfare of the youth of the whole world, we have prepared the roadmap 2029
By 2029 we will collectively succeed in uprooting the drug trade from India
Neither will we allow a single gram of drugs to enter India, nor will we allow a single gram of drugs to go out of India, this is the aim to move ahead
We have to fight together and win by making the fight against drugs a top priority with compassion
In this fight against drugs, we are moving towards complete victory by setting TARGET, TIMELINE and ACCOUNTABILITY
Now we have to go from MEETING to MISSION, REPORTING to RESULT, SEIZURE to END OF NETWORK and CASE to CONVICTION
Our goal should be to make ANTF an Anti Narco Mission Command
Move forward with the aim of dismantling the network instead of a Seizure-centric approach
District will have to be made the basic unit of fight against drugs
Nashamukt Mitras will visit 10 lakh schools, colleges and institutions of the country to create awareness among the youth and sensitize the campus directors
Along with backward-forward investigation, financial investigation and finding digital links should be our priority
The cartel has to be attacked at three levels - entry point, interstate distribution system and local cell network in the districts
The districts will be divided into three clusters – drug manufacturing or entry districts, transportation corridor districts and consumption districts
A campaign will have to be launched to send back the foreign accused present in India and blacklist them, so that they cannot come to India again
The fugitives who are supplying drugs to the country from abroad should be caught and brought before the Indian courts
Make the entire process of converting every ANTF information into actionable intelligence a part of your state's police culture
Union Home Minister launched TVCs for anti-narcotics awareness, launched NCB website and laid foundation stone of new zonal complexes of NCB in Lucknow and Dehradun
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 5:54PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today inaugurated the 3rd National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) Heads of States/UTs in New Delhi. On this occasion, the Union Home Minister launched Television Commercials (TVCs) to spread awareness against narcotic substances and laid the foundation stone of new zonal complexes of the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) in Lucknow and Dehradun. During the event, the best-performing ANTF of States and UTs were also honoured. In addition, the Union Home Minister launched the newly designed website of the NCB. In the two-day conference organised by the NCB, ANTF heads from 36 States and Union Territories, along with representatives of concerned government departments and other stakeholders, are participating.

In his address, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, we have for the past five years been taking one step after another in an effort to achieve the difficult goal of a drug free India. He said that the time has now come to deliver a decisive blow against narcotics, which have become the most serious threat to the country and the world, and to achieve victory through collective efforts. Shri Shah said that by 31 December 2029, we will collectively succeed in uprooting the drug trade from India.

Shri Amit Shah said that in the past five years we have achieved success against several challenges such as terrorism in Kashmir, insurgency in the Northeast and the problem of Naxalism. The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) with the cooperation of all the states, we have ended these major problems that have confronted the country for decades. He said that the fight against drugs is the most difficult of all battles, but we cannot abandon this fight. Shri Shah said that to build a Viksit Bharat by 2047, to save future generations and to connect the youth with India’s development, the only option before us is to make India drug-free. We will have to fight this problem unitedly and with passion, and we must achieve victory.

Union Home Minister said that the ‘Vision Document 2026-2029’ is like the Gita for all those involved in this fight. This Vision Document has been prepared with great effort after discussions with more than 35 departments. He said that we have prepared the complete roadmap after taking suggestions from all stakeholders, and it has been given to everyone with definite targets. Targets and timelines have also been fixed in it. The Home Minister said that it will also be reviewed after some time. Shri Shah added that the MHA or the NCB cannot do all this alone. We all have to fight this battle with top priority and complete dedication, and we have to win it as well.

Shri Amit Shah said that it should be our shared responsibility and resolve to end this menace of drugs that is hollowing out future generations. Our resolve should be that we will not allow even one gram of drugs to enter the country from anywhere in the world, nor will even one gram of drugs go from our country to the world. He said that we have prepared this roadmap with a resolve for the welfare of youth across the world. Shri Shah said that we will have to work for a drug-free India with sensitivity, with an understanding of its importance, and as the topmost priority. He said – Meet once the parents and siblings of even one young person afflicted by drugs. Until you meet them, intensity in this fight cannot arise in you. A weeping, wailing mother, a younger sister, and a boy who ranked in the top 10 in the Class 10 board examination is slowly moving towards death, while his helpless parents watch. There can be no greater sorrow than this for anyone, and for us too it is a national loss. A talented child who was going to contribute to India’s development in the days to come - his life is ending midway. There can be no greater loss than this for us and for the country.

Union Home Minister said that we have to fight the battle against drugs with clarity. He said that the focal points of this fight have already been identified, and a roadmap has also been prepared at the state level to take intelligence, investigation, financial action and prosecution in one direction. Shri Shah said that in the first ANTF conference we had created an institutional mechanism and strengthened it. In the second ANTF conference, we discussed capability, action and execution in order to convert that mechanism into action. Today, the third ANTF conference will convert this roadmap into a decisive battle.

Shri Amit Shah said that whatever we have done so far is not enough. Until the Principal of every school, the Patwari of the village, the PSI of the police station, the Director General of Police and the Chief Secretary of the state, and even the Home Secretary of the Government of India, work in one direction, we will not achieve success. He said that today’s conference is the most important because this time we will move forward towards complete victory by fixing Target, Timeline and Accountability.

Union Home Minister said that we now have to move from Meeting to Mission, from Reporting to Result, from Seizure to the dismantling of Networks, and from Case to Conviction. He said that until all departments of the state governments and the Government of India engage in this work, we cannot move forward.

Shri Amit Shah said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has set the target of building a Viksit Bharat by August 15, 2047 before the 140 crore citizens of the country, when India will be at the forefront globally in every sector. He said that if we are to achieve this goal, we cannot do so with a youth power and future generation hollowed out by addiction. He stated that India is the youngest country in the world, which is why the threat is also the largest for us in the global context. This is our necessity because the health, skills, labour, and thinking capacity of the youth alone can lead the country to that goal, and drugs damage all four of these capacities.

Union Home Minister said that for emerging challenges such as synthetic drugs, diversion of precursor chemicals, new communication technologies, dark-net, drug markets, crypto, dead-drop delivery systems, and international drug networks, a team of officers who think 'out-of-the-box' should be constituted in every state, and success should be shared and implemented across the entire nation.

Shri Amit Shah stated that the Vision Document 2026–2029 rests on four pillars: Enforcement, intelligence & operations, Control of precursor & synthetic drugs, Demand & harm reduction, and Capacity building & coordination. Over 100 targets have been categorized across these four pillars. Under the target of registering 1 lakh Nashamukt Mitras outlined in the Vision Document, various ministries have registered 46,780 Nashamukt Mitras so far, and they are already operational. To take this campaign to the grassroots level, Nashamukt Mitras will visit 10 lakh schools, colleges, and institutions across the country in the coming days to caution the youth and sensitize campus directors.

Shri Amit Shah said that today we are discussing converting the roadmap into results, and the most crucial element of the brainstorming taking place over these two days is compassion. Our goal should be to transform the ANTF into an ‘Anti-Narco Mission Command’, and State Chief Secretaries will need to adopt a different approach regarding manpower, technology, budget, and other resources. The Home Minister added that the Government of India is emphasizing technology and forensics in capacity building.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation stated that instead of maintaining a seizure-centric approach, we must move forward with the objective of dismantling entire networks. Our priority, along with backward-forward investigation, must also include financial investigation and tracing digital links. Our strike must hit the funds earned by drug dealers. Shri Shah said that cartels must be targeted at three levels: the entry point, the inter-state distribution system, and the local sales networks within districts. Further, districts will be categorized into three clusters: those where drugs are manufactured or enter the country, those serving as transportation corridors, and those where consumption takes place.

Union Home Minister stated that we must increase the utilization of PITNDPS, as there is a strong need for it in the country. A complete roadmap from investigation to conviction must be formulated in coordination with public prosecutors. A dedicated campaign must be launched to deport foreign accused present in India and blacklist them so they can never re-enter the country. Moreover, the fugitives who are supplying drugs to the country from abroad should be caught and brought before the Indian courts. By targeting borders and production centres, all loopholes must be plugged. Every ANTF should integrate the entire process of converting information to actionable intelligence into the work culture of their respective state police force. The Home Minister expressed confidence that we will succeed in this fight against drugs and emerge victorious.

Participation in this national conference will assist states, departments, and agencies under the 'Whole of Government Approach' to move forward with renewed resolve to effectively combat drug trafficking across the country over the next three years.

The deliberations held during the conference will help strengthen the effective enforcement of drug control laws and make the strategies adopted to protect the country's youth from drugs more impactful. This national event will provide an effective platform to bolster a future-ready partnership between the NCB and ANTFs of States and Union Territories to tackle drug abuse and fulfil the pledge of a Nasha Mukt Bharat.

'Swachhata Hi Seva 2026': Department of Fertilizers Empowers Workforce to Champion Circular Economy
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 5:54PM by PIB Delhi

To streamline institutional initiatives and maximize on-ground impact during the nationwide "Swachhata Hi Seva" (SHS) Campaign 2026 (being observed from September 17 to October 2, 2026), a comprehensive review and sensitization meeting was convened on September 22, 2026, at 11:00 AM under the chairmanship of the Senior Economic Advisor, Department of Fertilizers (DoF), Government of India, Shri Kuntal Sensarma.

The meeting witnessed wide institutional participation from key stakeholders across the sector, including officers of the Department of Fertilizers, representatives from the Fertilizer Industry Coordination Committee (FICC), and senior management executives, plant heads and designated Swachhata Nodal Officers from all Fertilizer PSUs, Cooperatives, and Joint Venture/Private Fertilizer Companies. The primary objective of the session was to evaluate the impact of the initial kick-off phase launched on September 17 and enforce unified alignment across administrative headquarters, manufacturing plants, and field formations to drive mass public and employee mobilization.

Focus on Five Core Thematic Pillars:

Following directions emerging from high-level inter-ministerial deliberations, the Chair emphasized the disciplined execution of 11 dated activities categorized under five foundational thematic pillars across all units and townships:

  • Swachhata Hi Seva: Intensive, end-to-end cleaning and beautification drives across office premises, workstation cubicles, residential quarters, plants, and adjacent public areas, with special emphasis on sites of cultural, historical, and tourism importance.
  • Kabaad Se Kala (Art from Waste): Creative initiatives encouraging personnel to repurpose office and industrial waste into functional, aesthetic, or artistic installations. Aimed at reducing carbon footprints, reusing resources, and institutionalizing circular-economy principles, departmental staff and PSU units have been invited to submit their innovative entries by September 28, 2026.
  • Khel & Khel Bhawana: Organizing sports meets, fitness challenges, and community games—particularly on holidays—to foster health, discipline, teamwork, and an active lifestyle among employees, their families, and children.
  • Samvad: Hosting interactive seminars, expert discussions, and awareness dialogues centred on water conservation, ecological balance, and sustainable environmental practices to drive institutional and personal behavioural change.
  • Gyan Yatra: Conducting community awareness marches and rallies featuring informative placards to propagate core messages on sanitation, environmental stewardship, and civic responsibility, actively involving youth and local communities.

National Culmination: 'Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath' on October 1:

A critical directive was issued for the national mega-event scheduled for October 1, 2026. All fertilizer PSUs, cooperatives, industrial units, and field offices were instructed to ensure 100% workforce participation for the voluntary cleanliness drive under the national banner “Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath”, dedicating one full hour of synchronized Shramdaan across all installations.

Employee Ideation and Periodic Safai Audits:

In line with earlier operational directives, senior officers of the Department are undertaking periodic 'Safai Audits' to inspect sanitation standards and sustain cleanliness benchmarks. To promote participatory governance from the ground up, the Department continues to run the 'Ek Sujaav Swachhata Ki Or' initiative, actively encouraging personnel to submit innovative, practical ideas to enhance workplace hygiene and administrative efficiency.

Real-Time Digital Monitoring & National Reporting:

To guarantee operational transparency and measurable outcomes, all participating entities were directed to upload high-resolution photographic evidence, short video documentation, and performance metrics on a daily basis directly onto the dedicated SHS-2026 Portal. Concurrently, units will maintain real-time reporting via the official institutional WhatsApp network. All uploaded field metrics will flow directly into the centralized repository for National-Level Performance Reporting, with comprehensive consolidated dossiers to be submitted by October 7, 2026.

The Department of Fertilizers reiterates that the sustained success of the Swachhata mission rests upon the dedication and active participation of its personnel, driving a cleaner, greener, and more responsive administrative environment.

2313530.title: From Greenery to Prosperity with NSFDC-WBSCDC Support
2313530.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Greenery to Prosperity with NSFDC-WBSCDC Support
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 5:06PM by PIB Delhi

Timely institutional support can help women organise themselves, build sustainable livelihoods and improve the well-being of their families. Whileas limited access to affordable finance often prevents rural women from starting income-generating activities and achieving economic independence.

Maa Lakshmi Mahila Samiti, an 11-member Self-Help Group in Purulia district, West Bengal, transformed its livelihood through greenhouse farming with financial assistance of Rs. 1 lakh under NSFDC's Mahila Samriddhi Yojana. The loan was disbursed through WBSCDC on 5 February 2025.

Before receiving the assistance, the members had no regular source of income and faced financial uncertainty. Despite their willingness to work, limited access to capital prevented them from starting a sustainable livelihood activity.

The members learned about the scheme through the district office of the West Bengal Scheduled Castes Development Corporation. They subsequently applied for financial assistance to undertake greenhouse farming on leased land. The loan provided the capital required to begin cultivation and establish a collective source of livelihood.

Through sustained effort and cooperation, the group successfully developed its greenhouse farming activity. Each member now earns approximately Rs. 4,000 to Rs. 8,000 per month. The additional income has improved the economic condition of their families and enabled them to meet household needs with greater confidence.

Today, the members of Maa Lakshmi Mahila Samiti are moving forward with greater self-confidence and financial independence. Their journey demonstrates how timely credit and institutional support can empower rural women to create sustainable livelihoods. The group has expressed its gratitude to NSFDC and WBSCDC for supporting its journey towards prosperity and self-reliance.

2313522.title: Prime Minister celebrates World Rhino Day
2313522.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister celebrates World Rhino Day
PM shares initiation of Project Rhino
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 4:58PM by PIB Delhi
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today celebrated the magnificent greater one-horned rhinoceros on the occasion of World Rhino Day and lauded all those at the forefront of its protection. He noted that Assam now holds nearly 80 percent of the world’s rhino population and that Kaziranga’s efforts to end rhino poaching have been extensively appreciated.

The Prime Minister highlighted that rhinos have either returned or are well protected in parts of Bihar and West Bengal, while the successful reintroduction of rhinos in Dudhwa, Uttar Pradesh, is creating history. He stated that this demonstrates the sustained commitment of the people towards animal protection and active wildlife management in the range states. Furthermore, to take species conservation forward in the country, he shared that Project Rhino has been initiated to provide financial and technical support to the range states for protection, habitat management, genetic improvement, and understanding population dynamics.

In a post on X, the Prime Minister wrote:

"On World Rhino Day, we celebrate the magnificent greater one-horned rhinoceros and laud all those at the forefront of its protection.

Assam now holds nearly 80% of the world’s rhino population and Kaziranga’s efforts to end rhino poaching have been extensively appreciated.

On one hand, rhinos have either returned or are well protected in parts of Bihar and West Bengal. On the other hand, success of reintroduction of rhinos in Dudhwa (Uttar Pradesh) is creating history. This shows the sustained commitment of our people towards animal protection and active wildlife management in the range states.

Taking species conservation in the country forward, I am happy to share that Project Rhino has been initiated for financial and technical support to the range states for protection, habitat management, genetic improvement and understanding population dynamics."

2313520.title: NHAI Signs MoU with SSNNL to Simplify Approval Framework for National Highway and Irrigation Infrastructure Projects in Gujarat
2313520.body_html:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
NHAI Signs MoU with SSNNL to Simplify Approval Framework for National Highway and Irrigation Infrastructure Projects in Gujarat
MoU aims to strengthen inter-departmental coordination, facilitate faster approvals and ensure seamless execution of National Highway and Irrigation infrastructure projects
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 4:55PM by PIB Delhi

To strengthen inter-agency coordination and expedite infrastructure development, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam Limited (SSNNL) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to establish a simplified and time-bound framework for granting approvals for National Highway, canal and pipeline crossings across the State of Gujarat. The MoU aims to strengthen inter-departmental coordination, facilitate faster approvals and ensure seamless execution of National Highway and Irrigation infrastructure projects. The MoU was signed by Regional Officer-Gandhinagar, NHAI and Chief Engineer (QC, Tech. & CPC), SSNNL in presence of Directors from SSNNL and other officials at Gandhinagar, Gujarat.

A key feature of the MoU is mutual waiver of various fees, charges and other levies by NHAI and SSNNL for all National Highway, canal and pipeline crossings covered under the agreement. This provision will help in reducing project costs, eliminate avoidable procedural bottlenecks and optimize the utilization of public funds to accelerate the pace of infrastructure development.

The MoU also lays down a framework for early sharing of project information, adoption of standardized engineering practices as well as clearly defined responsibilities for the construction and maintenance of crossing structures. These measures will facilitate better project planning and ensure adherence to high standards of quality and operational efficiency.

The MoU marks a significant milestone in promoting integrated infrastructure planning in Gujarat by fostering closer coordination between NHAI and SSNL. The collaborative framework will accelerate the implementation of both National Highways and irrigation infrastructure projects in Gujarat, while improving efficiency, implementation timelines and reducing overall financial implication associated with project execution.

By enabling faster approvals and strengthening coordination, the MoU reinforces NHAI’s commitment to develop world-class infrastructure that not only enhances connectivity but also supports economic growth.
