2312067.title: Swachh Sagar Surakshit Sagar Has Evolved into a Whole-of-Government, Whole-of-Society Movement for Clean Coasts and Safe Seas: Dr. Jitendra Singh
2312067.body_html:
Ministry of Earth Sciences
Swachh Sagar Surakshit Sagar Has Evolved into a Whole-of-Government, Whole-of-Society Movement for Clean Coasts and Safe Seas: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Leads Coastal Clean-Up Drive at Juhu Beach on Eve of International Coastal Cleanup Day, highlights India's unexplored ocean wealth and refers to Deep Ocean Mission launched by PM Sh Narendra Modi as the torchbearer of India's Blue Economy
India’s Coastal Clean-Up Campaign Unites Government, Citizens and Public Figures for Cleaner Seas: Dr. Jitendra Singh
From 75-Day Campaign to Nationwide Movement: Swachh Sagar Surakshit Sagar Expands Public Participation in Ocean Conservation: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Campaign Mobilises Coastal States and Union Territories, Central Agencies, Students, Volunteers, NGOs, Celebrities and Sporting Personalities Across the Country
Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 4:39PM by PIB Delhi

 Leading the coastal clean-up drive at Juhu Beach on the eve of "International Coastal Cleanup Day" being observed across the world tomorrow, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and MoS in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh highlighted India's unexplored ocean wealth and referred to Deep Ocean Mission launched by PM Sh Narendra Modi as the torchbearer of India's Blue Economy.

The Minister said that the ‘Swachh Sagar Surakshit Sagar’ campaign, launched in 2022 during the celebrations of India’s 75th year of Independence, has evolved into a whole-of-government and whole-of-society movement for cleaner coasts and safer seas.

What began as a 75-day inter-ministerial campaign has grown into an annual nationwide initiative around International Coastal Cleanup Day, observed on the third Saturday of September, bringing together government institutions and citizens in a collective effort to protect India’s coastal and marine environment. The 2026 campaign is being conducted from September 12 to 19.

Dr. Jitendra Singh led the coastal clean-up programme at Juhu Beach, Mumbai, organised on the eve of International Coastal Cleanup Day. Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, Dr. T. Srinivasa Kumar Tummala, and BCCI President Mithun Manhas were among those present, along with Directors and senior officials of the Ministry of Earth Sciences and its institutions, public representatives, celebrities, volunteers and other participants. The programme included a mass Ocean Pledge, followed by a hands-on clean-up activity in which Dr. Jitendra Singh joined officials and volunteers in removing plastic and other waste from the shoreline.

The campaign has brought together coastal States and Union Territories, State Governments, Central Government departments and agencies, the Indian Coast Guard, Indian Navy, students, NGOs, volunteers and local communities. Celebrities, public representatives and sporting personalities have also joined the initiative, giving the campaign a wider social reach. The participation of BCCI President Mithun Manhas at Juhu Beach this year further reflected the effort to bring diverse sections of society together for ocean conservation.

The initiative is rooted in India’s growing engagement with its vast maritime domain. Following Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s announcement of the Deep Ocean Mission from the Red Fort, India has been strengthening its scientific and technological capabilities to explore the deep ocean and understand its resources and ecosystems. The oceans hold significant potential in terms of metals and minerals, fisheries, marine biodiversity and bioresources, making scientific exploration, responsible use and conservation of marine resources important for India’s long-term development.

The Minister said that the benefits of India’s maritime resources can be realised only alongside protection of the health of marine ecosystems. Cleaner beaches, reduced plastic pollution and greater public awareness are therefore essential to maintaining healthy oceans and ensuring sustainable use of marine resources. The campaign seeks to turn this awareness into sustained citizen participation and collective action.

India’s coastline of about 11,098 km extends across its coastal States and Union Territories and supports diverse ecosystems, communities and economic activities. Its scale calls for coordinated action by governments, scientific institutions, coastal communities and citizens to address marine litter and protect fragile coastal ecosystems.

The 2026 edition of ‘Swachh Sagar Surakshit Sagar’, being conducted from September 12 to 19, features coastal clean-up drives and a range of public-engagement activities across the country. The campaign is bringing together citizens, students, coastal communities, educational institutions, NGOs, volunteer organisations and government agencies as part of a nationwide effort to promote ocean conservation and responsible environmental practices. The Ministry of Earth Sciences and its institutions are supporting the campaign through scientific and public-outreach initiatives related to marine litter and coastal environmental protection.

Citizen participation is also being strengthened through the Sagar Prahari platform, which enables public engagement with the campaign and supports documentation of marine litter. The initiative complements the larger objective of combining scientific understanding with public participation in addressing marine pollution and protecting coastal ecosystems.

The Juhu Beach programme brought together government representatives, sporting personalities, public figures, volunteers and citizens in a common effort to protect India’s coastline. The mass pledge and clean-up activity reinforced the message that keeping India’s shores clean and its seas safe is a shared responsibility, requiring sustained participation well beyond a single day or campaign.

The ‘Swachh Sagar Surakshit Sagar’ campaign continues to build on the spirit of collective action with which it was launched during India’s 75th year of Independence, strengthening public participation for cleaner beaches, healthier oceans and a more sustainable maritime future.

2312061.title: Union Environment Minister reviews Uttar Pradesh's Air Pollution Action Plan for Delhi-NCR, with Chief Minister (UP)
2312061.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2312061.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Union Environment Minister reviews Uttar Pradesh's Air Pollution Action Plan for Delhi-NCR, with Chief Minister (UP)
Shri Bhupender Yadav stresses Strict Enforcement, Accelerated Implementation and Whole-of-Society approach to curb Air Pollution in a time-bound manner
Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 4:34PM by PIB Delhi

Lucknow/New Delhi, 18th September, 2026

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today held a comprehensive review meeting with Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, Shri Yogi Adityanath, and senior officials of the State Government in Lucknow to assess the progress of ongoing measures aimed at improving air quality in Delhi-NCR. Union Minister of State for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Kirtivardhan Singh, Uttar Pradesh Minister for Environment and Forest Dr. Arun Kumar, and State Minister of Transport (Independent charge) Shri Dayashankar Singh were also present during the meeting.

Addressing the meeting, Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath welcomed the measures being taken by the Government to curb air pollution in Delhi NCR. He directed all State Government officials to take timely action on different measures discussed during the meeting. He further thanked the Union Minister for organizing this review meeting and his valuable guidance in this matter.

During the meeting, Shri Bhupender Yadav emphasized the need for accelerated implementation, stronger inter-agency coordination and strict enforcement to ensure substantial reduction in air pollution levels before the onset of the winter season. Emphasizing the urgency of timely action, the Minister said, "The window before the winter season must be fully utilized to implement pollution control measures in mission mode. Timely execution, effective coordination and strict enforcement will be critical to achieving visible improvements in Delhi-NCR's air quality."

Reviewing measures to curb Road Dust, Shri Yadav requested that end-to-end paving and greening of roads with local species shrubs/grasses during monsoons be undertaken on priority, with focused attention on pothole identification and repair, construction of footpaths and pavements, roadside greening and deep cleaning of roads. He urged that all gaps in the deployment of Mechanical Road Sweeping Machines (MRSMs) be bridged at the earliest, while suggesting that all MRSMs be geo-tagged to facilitate real-time monitoring of road-cleaning operations and improve accountability.

Reviewing the status of Electric Mobility, the Minister stressed that deployment of electric buses and installation of EV charging stations across the NCR municipal corporations in Uttar Pradesh should be expedited, noting significant gaps in the existing fleet. He congratulated the Uttar Pradesh Government for the rapidly increasing tree covered area across the State. On the issue of End-of-Life (EoL) vehicles, Shri Yadav requested that the authorities expedite issuance of No Objection Certificates (NOCs) for transfer of eligible EoL vehicles outside the NCR, while simultaneously encouraging scientific scrapping of old and unfit vehicles. He also called for faster replacement of old polluting vehicles with electric vehicles under the Parivartan Scheme. The Minister requested that Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) system be installed at all fuel stations for effective implementation of the "No PUCC, No Fuel" initiative. Stressing the need to improve urban traffic management, Shri Yadav asked the authorities to identify Traffic Congestion Hotspots on a mission mode and implement suitable mitigation measures at the earliest.

Reviewing Industrial Pollution control measures, Shri Yadav emphasized the need for accelerated installation of Online Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (OCEMS) and Air Pollution Control Devices (APCDs) across industrial units. The Union Minister reviewed progress on Construction and Demolition Waste management and requested that establishment of Secondary Collection Centres for C&D waste be expedited. Referring to Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) and Biomass Burning, he stressed that liquidation of Legacy Waste should be undertaken on a war footing. On Stubble Burning, Shri Yadav requested the State Government to bridge gaps in procurement of Crop Residue Management (CRM) machinery. He emphasized the need for intensive Information, Education and Communication (IEC) campaigns and farmer training programmes to promote effective use of CRM equipment.

Underscoring the importance of Public Participation and coordinated institutional action, Shri Yadav said that air pollution can be effectively tackled only through a 'Whole of Government' and 'Whole of Society' approach. The Union Minister stressed on strict implementation of the advisories issued by the government to curb air pollution. He also emphasized increasing sanitation workers commensurate with the ratio of population. The Minister said that air pollution can be controlled only by following rules, using the latest technology and introducing innovation to tackle the issue. Extending a call for widespread public engagement, he stressed that all citizens must come forward to join hands with the authorities and play an important part in this fight against air pollution.

The meeting was attended by Secretary, MoEFCC, Shri Tanmay Kumar; Chairperson, Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), Shri Rajesh Verma; senior officers of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and the Government of Uttar Pradesh. Senior officials from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and the Uttar Pradesh State Pollution Control Board (UPSPCB) were also present.

2312013.title: WOAH PVS–PPP Targeted Support Workshop on “FMD-Free Zone Development in India” concludes with focus on strengthening State Action Plans and Public–Private Partnerships
2312013.ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
2312013.body_html:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
WOAH PVS–PPP Targeted Support Workshop on “FMD-Free Zone Development in India” concludes with focus on strengthening State Action Plans and Public–Private Partnerships
Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 3:56PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India, in collaboration with the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), organised a three-day PVS–PPP Targeted Support Workshop on “FMD-Free Zone Development in India” from 15–17 September 2026 at the National Agricultural Science Complex (NASC), New Delhi. The workshop brought together representatives from the DAHD, 12 State Animal Husbandry Departments, experts from WOAH, Paris, CDDL/RDDLs, NDDB, ICAR Research Institutions, industry, livestock value-chain stakeholders and technical experts to strengthen the pathway towards establishing FMD-free zones and compartments in India.

The workshop was aimed at supporting national and state stakeholders in refining and strengthening their FMD-free zone and compartment action plans through technical analysis, peer learning, public–private partnership (PPP) design and alignment with WOAH standards and official recognition requirements.

The Inaugural Session was graced by Shri. Naresh Pal Gangwar, Secretary, AHD and WOAH Delegate of India in presence of Dr Naveena B. Maheswarappa, Animal Husbandry Commissioner, DAHD, Dr Divakar Hemadri, ADG (Animal Health), ICAR, New Delhi and Ms. Barbara Alessandrini, Head, Capacity Building Department, WOAH, Paris. 

Shri. Naresh Pal Gangwar, Secretary, AHD in his address highlighted India’s journey for FMD Control in India. He informed that, India has made substantial progress in FMD control under the Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme. Under the Government’s flagship FMD control programme, the country has invested in large-scale vaccination, animal identification, surveillance, laboratory strengthening and disease reporting. He mentioned about the Department’s objective under the Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme to control and ultimately obtain FMD freedom by 2030.  Administration of more than 147.16 crore FMD vaccine doses till date, benefiting around 8.04 crore farmers and decline in FMD outbreaks from 132 in 2019 to 40 in 2025 and 20 till August 2026 and decline in NSP antibody positivity to 8.1% in 2025 were also highlighted.

He also informed that this workshop is a continuation of the WOAH PVS-PPP Targeted Support which was held in India during 2025 and thanked WOAH for their continued partnership and technical support through the PVS–PPP Targeted Support programme. He further added that the Department has developed the guidelines for creation of FMD free compartments in India with extensive rounds of consultation with stakeholders. Further the Department for the first time has also come up with the Minimum Standards of Veterinary Infrastructure in India in 2025 and the Department is supporting the States under the Support to States for Capital Investment (SASCI) framework, to address infrastructure and system-readiness gaps identified by States. He also urged to have a discussion on the emerging threat of SAT Serotypes of FMD and highlighted India’s preparedness to deal with such exotic serotypes.

He emphasised that, India has demonstrated a sustained national FMD control and the next step is to prove and maintain freedom in defined populations. With WOAH's technical guidance and the combined efforts of States, Veterinary Services, laboratories, industry and exporters, we can build FMD-free zones and compartments that are scientifically credible, operationally sustainable, digitally traceable and capable of supporting greater confidence and trade.

On the first day WOAH experts provided an overview of the WOAH Performance of Veterinary Services (PVS) Pathway and the PVS–PPP approach, WOAH requirements for recognition of FMD-free zones, surveillance and post-vaccination monitoring, international experience from Brazil, and opportunities for public–private engagement.

A key component of the workshop was a series of practical group exercises involving public and private stakeholders from the nine priority States. The second day focused on co-designing solutions to address identified bottlenecks. Discussions covered vaccination systems and engagement with the vaccine industry, surveillance and diagnostic partnerships, animal identification and traceability, producer organisations and value-chain integration, as well as investment and financing models.

The final day focused on validation of State-level action plans. Representatives of the nine priority States presented their proposed action plans, followed by technical feedback from WOAH experts and other specialists. The presentations provided an opportunity to refine interventions related to surveillance, vaccination, laboratory preparedness, traceability, biosecurity, movement control, veterinary infrastructure and PPP engagement.

The workshop emphasised that PPP engagement should extend beyond financial participation and encompass the full animal-health value chain, including vaccine supply and delivery, diagnostics, animal identification and traceability, producer organisations, dairy and livestock value chains, veterinary service delivery and risk communication. The approach is intended to create stronger ownership, accountability and sustainability of FMD-free zone initiatives.

The three-day deliberations culminated in the refinement of State Action Plans and identification of priority technical interventions and opportunities for public–private partnership (PPP) in FMD-free zone and compartment development. In the concluding session, Dr. Naveena B. Maheswarappa, Animal Husbandry Commissioner, expressed appreciation for the valuable technical guidance provided by the WOAH team of experts and acknowledged the active participation and constructive contributions of the State Animal Husbandry Departments and other stakeholders.

Dr. Maheswarappa expressed confidence that the States would translate the outcomes of the workshop into clear, evidence-based and time-bound action plans for the progressive development of FMD-free zones and compartments, with strengthened collaboration and meaningful engagement of the private sector.

 The initiative represents an important step towards India's national objective of achieving FMD-free status by 2030. The strengthened State Action Plans, supported by WOAH standards and appropriately designed public–private partnerships, are expected to provide a structured pathway for progressive development, maintenance and eventual recognition of FMD-free zones and compartments in India.

Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Pharmaceuticals
Special Campaign 6.0 from 2nd October to 31st October, 2026
E-Waste Management, Grievance Redressal and Field Office Outreach to Drive Special Campaign 6.0
Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 3:47PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, along with the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), seven National Institutes of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (NIPERs), Pharmaceutical & Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI) and Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) – Bengal Chemical & Pharmaceutical Ltd. The initiative aims to institutionalize Swachhata culture and streamline government functioning by eliminating office pendency.

The campaign is structured in two operational phases:

  2. Implementation Phase (2nd – 31st October 2026) : Execution of cleanliness drives, scrap disposal, and grievance redressal.

Focus Areas for Special Campaign 6.0 :

  • E-Waste Management : Safe collection, segregation, and disposal of electronic scrap in accordance with E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022.
  • Grievance & Reference Resolution : Accelerated disposal of pending MP References, State Government Communications, PMO References, Parliamentary Assurances, Public Grievances, and CPGRAMS Appeals.
  • Field Office Outreach : Active participation from field offices, PSUs and NIPERs to conduct outdoor cleanliness drives, office beautification, and sustainability drives.

Through these measures, the Department of Pharmaceuticals reaffirms its commitment to transparent governance, efficient public service delivery and sustainable office management.

2311993.title: India advancing towards Viksit Bharat@2047 with resilience, strength, innovation, inclusive development & compassion: Raksha Mantri
2311993.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
India advancing towards Viksit Bharat@2047 with resilience, strength, innovation, inclusive development & compassion: Raksha Mantri
Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 3:29PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has said that the Government is serving the nation with a special focus on fostering resilience, determination, compassion, innovation, strength, inclusive prosperity and a strong sense of national identity among citizens to realise the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047. Addressing an event in Kochi, Keralam, on September 18, 2026, he asserted that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India is advancing on the path of development by drawing inspiration from India’s centuries-old values such as courage to persevere, security and protection of citizens, spirit of service, determination to achieve goals, compassion, inspiring future generations, strengthening national capabilities, and ensuring inclusive prosperity & global leadership.

Raksha Mantri highlighted that before 2014, India faced significant challenges such as corruption and misgovernance which had weakened the morale of the people, and the nation’s progress in the last 12 years has been shaped by its ability to face adversity with confidence and convert challenges into opportunities. “Over the last 12 years, the world has faced a pandemic such as COVID-19 and witnessed several wars, which have had a profound impact on the global economy. Despite global challenges, we are moving steadily on the path towards becoming a self-reliant and developed nation,” he said.

Reiterating the Government’s commitment towards the protection and security of citizens from evil forces, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that Operation Sindoor is proof of India’s willingness to cross the border to eliminate those who threaten the sovereignty and integrity of the country. He added that Naxalism, too, has been brought to an end.

On the Government’s aim to continuously bolster indigenous capabilities, Raksha Mantri stated that indigenous defence production, which was just Rs 40,000 crore in 2014, has now reached nearly Rs 1.80 lakh crore. He added that defence exports have risen from nearly Rs 600 crore to around Rs 40,000 crore, with Indian equipment reaching around 100 countries.

Voicing the nation’s resolve to work tirelessly towards its goals with courage and determination, Shri Rajnath Singh described youth as the country’s greatest strength. “Our youth are building start-ups, creating unicorns, developing drones, building hydrogen trains, and making rockets and satellites. They are leaving no stone unturned to make India a developed nation,” he said.

Raksha Mantri added that guided by the virtue of compassion, the Government is working to improve the lives of the people, pointing out that over the past 10 to 12 years, more than 250 million people have been lifted out of poverty. He also stated that whether it is the success of India’s democracy or the success of its welfare schemes, India today serves as a source of inspiration to the world. He spoke about UPI, which is the world’s largest real-time payment system, and has been adopted by more than 11 countries. He mentioned the schemes such as PM SHRI, Ayushman Bharat, Lakhpati Didi, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, Jal Jeevan Mission, and Ujjwala Yojana, which have made development more inclusive.

Shri Rajnath Singh noted that India has become a source of hope for the world as it has achieved several targets set to fight climate change ahead of schedule, and provided free vaccines to the people in the country & sent more than 300 million vaccines to 100 countries during COVID-19. He stressed that India has emerged as a civilisational leader as today the world celebrates International Yoga Day. India is now providing leadership to the world through initiatives such as the International Solar Alliance and the Global Biofuels Alliance, he added.

Raksha Mantri underlined that India’s development journey is not limited to economic growth, but also involves strengthening national confidence and moving beyond the colonial mindset. Under PM Modi’s leadership, India is witnessing a cultural and civilisational renaissance, he said. Highlighting the importance of civilisational and cultural heritage, he stated that the country’s modernisation should go hand-in-hand with an appreciation of its cultural traditions. “’Sarva Dharma Samabhava’ or equal respect for all faiths has always been at the heart of our civilisational ethos. And yet, because of Western secularism, our Dharma was made to appear as communalism, tradition as backwardness, belief as fanaticism, and faith as superstition,” he added.

Shri Rajnath Singh emphasised the importance of making the younger generation more aware of India’s history, culture and heritage. Greater awareness among youth, he said, would contribute to stronger national consciousness and help build confidence in India’s place in the world. He called upon the youth to contribute to India’s economic, social and technological transformation, saying that a confident, capable and socially inclusive India can emerge as a developed nation and play a greater role in shaping the future of the world.

On the crucial role of media in today’s times, Raksha Mantri stated that journalism is rightly called the fourth pillar of democracy, terming an independent & impartial press as one of the strongest instruments for ensuring accountability. “The role of the media is not merely to report the news. It is also to ask difficult questions, bring the truth before the people, and hold those in power accountable,” he said.

2311987.title: BIMSTEC Energy Centre Organises Five-Day Capacity Building Programme on New & Emerging Technologies in Power Sector
2311987.body_html:
Ministry of Power
BIMSTEC Energy Centre Organises Five-Day Capacity Building Programme on New & Emerging Technologies in Power Sector
Programme brings together participants from seven BIMSTEC Member States for technical capacity building and knowledge sharing
Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 3:23PM by PIB Delhi

The BIMSTEC Energy Centre (BEC) organised a five-day Capacity Building Programme on “New & Emerging Technologies in Power Sector (Generation, Transmission, Distribution & End Use)” from 14 to 18 September 2026 in Bengaluru in hybrid mode under the aegis of Ministry of Power, Government of India.

The programme was inaugurated on 14 September 2026 by Sh. Ghanshyam Prasad, Executive Director, BEC and Chairperson, Central Electricity Authority (CEA), Government of India, along with Sh. Pankaj Kumar, Joint Secretary (Transmission), Ministry of Power, Government of India.

The Inaugural Session was also attended by Smt. J Sreedevi, Director General, Central Power Research Institute (CPRI), Sh. Asit Singh, Member Secretary, Southern Regional Power Committee (SRPC), Sh. M S Hejib, Executive Director, POWERGRID SRTS-II, and Sh. T Srinivas, Executive Director, Southern Regional Load Despatch Centre (SRLDC), GRID-INIDIA.

Participants from Bhutan, India, Sri Lanka and Thailand attended in person, while Bangladesh, Myanmar and the BIMSTEC Secretariat, Dhaka participated online. The programme provided a platform for technical capacity building, exchange of national experiences and sharing of best practices in the rapidly evolving power sector.

The programme covered key emerging technologies across the power sector, including Renewable Energy, Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), Green Hydrogen, Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage (CCUS), Long Duration Energy Storage, Small Modular Reactors (SMRs), Smart Grids, advanced grid operation technologies, Artificial Intelligence (AI) in power systems and the impact of Data Centre loads. Advanced transmission technologies such as FACTS, HTLS conductors, Dynamic Line Rating and Grid-Forming Converters, along with the India Energy Stack, were also covered.

The programme combined classroom sessions with technical and industrial visits to major power-sector facilities in and around Bengaluru, including the 2500MW HVDC Kolar POWERGRID Station, Ohmium International Green Hydrogen Electrolyzer Gigafactory, POWERGRID’s RTAMC, SRLDC/REMC Control Rooms, CPRI Laboratory Facilities and Hot Line Training Centre (HLTC), NPTI.

The programme concluded on 18 September 2026 with a Valedictory Session, in the presence of Sh. Bhagwan Sahay Bairwa, Chief Engineer, CEA. The session included sharing of key learnings, country perspectives and participant feedback, followed by certificates and acknowledgements.

The programme forms part of BEC’s continuing capacity-building and knowledge-sharing initiatives aimed at promoting regional energy cooperation among BIMSTEC Member States. This particular program provided a strong foundation for greater cooperation in power-system planning, renewable integration, energy storage, transmission technology, knowledge sharing and electricity trade in BIMSTEC Region.

About BIMSTEC Energy Centre (BEC)

The BEC became operational in Bengaluru on 1 April 2025 and serves as a Centre of Excellence for regional energy cooperation, promoting sustainable development, energy security and energy integration among BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi Sectoral and Technical Cooperation) Member States Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka & Thailand.

2311989.title: TRAI Strengthens Framework for Curbing Unsolicited Commercial Communications through Technology-Driven Enforcement and Enhanced Consumer Protection
2311989.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
TRAI Strengthens Framework for Curbing Unsolicited Commercial Communications through Technology-Driven Enforcement and Enhanced Consumer Protection
Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 3:22PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has amended the Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference Regulations, 2018 (TCCCPR, 2018) to further strengthen the regulatory framework for curbing Unsolicited Commercial Communications (UCC), protect consumers from spam and prevent misuse of telecom resources for sending UCC.

TRAI issued “Draft Telecom Commercial Communication Customer Preference (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026” for Consultation on 13th March 2026 to seek stakeholders' views on key regulatory amendments needed to strengthen the existing regulatory framework, enhance enforcement mechanisms and address emerging challenges in the prevention and regulation of UCC. The consultation focused on several vital issues, including leveraging AI/ML-based suspected UCC detection to aid in regulatory enforcement, strengthening mechanism for complaint-based action, expanding scope of explicit consent to accommodate legacy consents available with the entities, providing for appeal mechanism, strengthening the accountability of Senders and Telemarketers, regulating Application-to-Person (A2P) calls, strengthening safeguards against the misuse of Headers and Content Templates etc.

The comments and counter-comments on the draft regulations were received till 19th April, 2026, and 04th May, 2026, respectively. The Open House Discussion (OHD) with the stakeholders was held on 3rd June, 2026. After considering stakeholders’ feedback and carrying out detailed analysis, the Authority has introduced the Telecom Commercial Communication Customer Preference (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026 today.

SALIENT FEATURES OF THE AMENDMENTS

(i) Leveraging AI/ML-based suspected UCC detection to aid in regulatory enforcement

(a) Major Telecom Service Providers (TSPs) have already deployed AI/ML-based systems to detect suspected spam communications and alert the customers. The Authority also issued a Direction on 27th February, 2026 to the TSPs for using AI/ML-based intelligence on suspected UCC for inter-operator sharing and to carry out further investigation of suspected UCC senders.

(b) The provisions of the said Direction have been suitably incorporated into the TCCCPR, 2018 through the introduction of Regulation 21A which mandates the TSPs to identify the sender’s CLIs having a high probability of being used for sending UCC and share the information among the TSPs.

(c) Where five or more CLIs (Calling Line Identification) associated with a Sender are flagged within a period of ten days, further investigation and graded action will be initiated by the Access Providers, including KYC re-verification, physical verification, barring of outgoing services, and disconnection of telecom resource in cases of repeated violations and misuse of telecom resources.

(d) Special numbering series designated for commercial communications, including the 140xx, 1600xx and 1601xx series, shall not be flagged as suspected spam for recipients, thereby ensuring that legitimate commercial communications and government communications from the regulated series are not inadvertently missed. 

(ii) Regulation of Application-to-Person (A2P) calls

(a) Application-to-Person (A2P) calling is being used for bulk commercial communications due to its ability to automate and scale large volumes of calls, and therefore, there exists a potential for their misuse for making spam calls.

(b) Accordingly, to regulate such calling, the amendments have defined A2P calls as voice calls initiated by an application, software system or automated platform without direct human dialing, including using autodialing, robo-calls and pre-recorded/artificial voice technologies. It has been mandated that every entity using A2P calls must pre-declare such use to its TSP along with the details of CLIs to be used for making such calls. A2P calls made without the required prior declaration will be treated as UCC.

(c) To act as a deterrent, a termination charge of up to ₹0.05 per minute has been introduced to be levied by the Terminating Access Provider on the Originating Access Provider for A2P calls.

(d) A2P calls made through any numbering series designated by the Authority for regulated commercial calls, and Authority-authorized calls are exempted from termination charges.

(iii) Commercial Communications based on inquiry:

(a) Commercial communications may be sent to a customer on the basis of an inquiry made by the customer to the sender for goods or products or services, only for a period of seven days from the date of such inquiry.

(b) However, to prevent the misuse of such provision for sending spam, it has been mandated that such an inquiry shall be made in writing or through digital means, and shall be maintained in a verifiable form by the Sender.

(c) The amendment is intended primarily to facilitate e-Commerce and e-Service Platforms.

(iv) Introduction of Consumer Appeal Mechanism

(a) Consumers will now be able to prefer an appeal against the resolution of UCC complaints. The appeal may be preferred within 15 days before the Appellate Authority.

(b) Appeals will be resolved by the Appellate Authority as per the Telecom Consumers Complaint Redressal (TCCR) Regulations, 2012.

(c) The appeal may be preferred through any of the modes available for lodging UCC complaints i.e. through TRAI DND App, TSPs App/Portal, and call or SMS to 1909 besides the modes specified under TCCRR, 2012.

(v) Strengthening of Complaint-Based Action against UCC

(a) The existing regulations provide a complaint threshold of 5 or more unique complaints within a period of ten days to trigger action against the UCC Sender.

(b) To enable early identification of UCC senders and faster action against them, the amendments have mandated corroboration of the complaint data received from consumers with the data of Senders detected by service provider’s AI systems as suspected of sending UCC with high probability.

(c) Action will be triggered against the sender if there are 3 or more unique complaints within a period of ten days and the concerned Sender’s CLI is also flagged by the AI/ML-based system as suspected of sending UCC.

(d) Certain timelines prescribed under the complaint mechanism have been revised keeping in view the practical time required for implementation.

(vi) Expanded Scope of Explicit Consent

The definition of consent has been expanded to include legacy consents already available with the entities. The framework is being amended to enable the recognition and digitization of such legacy consents. However, the legacy consents shall be considered valid only where they have been obtained through verifiable means and are subsequently registered on the Digital Platform of the TSPs.

(vii) Strengthening Measures against Misuse of Headers and Content Templates

(a)  In cases involving misuse of Headers or Content Templates, the Originating Access Provider shall suspend the misused Headers or Content Templates, within six hours of becoming aware of such misuse, and issue a notice to the concerned Sender within the prescribed period.

(b) The concerned Sender shall be required to undertake specified remedial measures to prevent any further misuse, and file a complaint with the appropriate law enforcement agency. Where the misuse is attributed to a Telemarketer, all its telecom resources across the TSPs will be disconnected for a period of one year, along with blacklisting.

(viii) Essential conditions of Agreement between Access Providers and Senders/Telemarketers

(a) Under the regulatory framework, the TSPs have been obligated to ensure compliance of the regulatory provisions by the Senders and Telemarketer through contractual obligations between them.  However, it has been observed that TSPs many times do not put strict conditions in the agreements to ensure compliance by these entities, primarily due to competition issues.

(b) Accordingly, to have more effective action against the Senders and Telemarketers engaged in sending UCC, a new provision has been introduced whereby the Authority may prescribe the essential conditions that must mandatorily form part of these agreements between the Access Providers and the Senders/ Telemarketers.

(ix) Classification of Senders

There exists a variety of Senders based on considerations such as the criticality of the services and the sector to which a Sender belongs, the importance of the entity to the economy, scale of operations, extent of usage of telecom resources by the Sender, and the potential impact of suspending/ disconnecting telecom resources of the Sender on the consumers. A new regulation has been introduced whereby the Authority may classify the Senders into different categories and may specify differentiated sets of enforcement measures applicable to such categories of Senders for violations of the regulations.

(x) Prohibition on blanket blocking/tagging by Call Management Applications

(a) Call Management Applications (CMAs) are prohibited from blanket blocking, filtering, or spam tagging calls from number series designated by the Authority or the Central Government for commercial communication such as 1600xx/1601xx for service and transactional calls, and 140xx for regulated promotional calls, since such tagging, without the safeguards built into the regulatory mechanism, risks mislabeling genuine commercial communications and government communications as spam, which are otherwise important to customers. However, individual consumers retain full freedom to block, or filter calls on their own devices.

(b) To facilitate wider collation of data for action against spammers, it has also been mandated that no CMA shall offer the users to report any unsolicited commercial communication under any name such as spam, junk, etc. on its platform, unless the CMA sends such report to the DLT platform maintained by the Access Providers.

(xi) Digital Interface for VNOs with the DLT Platform

As Virtual Network Operators (VNOs) are also Access Provider under the regulatory framework, the Network Service Operator (NSO) will be required to provide the VNO a digital interface having real-time functionality with the DLT platform and other systems necessary for the VNO to discharge its obligations as an Access Provider under the Regulations. This will address the operational difficulty presently being faced by the VNOs with respect to the access to the DLT Platform.

The amendments are aimed at strengthening consumer confidence in the commercial communication ecosystem, ensuring greater accountability across stakeholders, and enabling more effective and timely action against misuse of telecom resources by the spammers.

For further information, Shri Deepak Sharma, Advisor (QoS-Il), TRAI, may be contacted at 011-20907760 or at email-id advqos@trai.gov.in

2311960.title: Government Relaxes Sugar Stockholding Limit for Bulk Consumers from 15 to 30 Days, Additional stock to be sourced exclusively from imported sugar under Advance Authorization Scheme (AAS) and Tariff Rate Quota (TRQ)
2311960.ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
2311960.body_html:
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
Government Relaxes Sugar Stockholding Limit for Bulk Consumers from 15 to 30 Days, Additional stock to be sourced exclusively from imported sugar under Advance Authorization Scheme (AAS) and Tariff Rate Quota (TRQ)
Retail Sugar Prices Decline by Around 10%; Government Urges Trader & wholesalers to Pass on Benefit of Lower Ex-Mill Prices to Consumers
Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 2:47PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has decided that the existing 15 days’ stockholding limit for bulk consumers is relaxed to 30 days, subject to the condition that the quantity of stock held beyond the existing 15 days’ limit, shall be sourced exclusively from sugar imported under Advance Authorisation Scheme (AAS) and Tariff Rate Quota (TRQ). The stockholding limit for purchase from the open market shall remain unchanged and will be restricted to 15 days’ consumption only. The government has also put in place a mechanism for the declaration and weekly disclosure of sugar stocks every Friday by bulk consumers through the Department of Food and Public Distribution's online portal @ https://foodstock.dfpd.gov.in/

The Government has held detailed consultations with major bulk consumers of sugar and their suggestions have been duly considered with a view to maintaining a stable and orderly sugar market.

At present, bulk consumers using or consuming more than 10 MT of sugar per month as a raw material for production, consumption or use are permitted to hold sugar stock for a period not exceeding 15 days of their consumption.  Bulk consumers have represented that the existing limit may be enhanced, particularly in view of the upcoming festival season. They also suggested that they may be permitted to directly source sugar from importers holding sugar imported under Advance Authorisation Scheme and Tariff Rate Quota, so as to ensure uninterrupted availability of sugar for industrial consumption without adversely affecting domestic supplies.

The measure is intended to strike a balance between the interests of bulk consumers and the need to maintain stability in the domestic sugar market. It will provide greater operational flexibility to genuine industrial consumers during the upcoming festival season while ensuring that additional stocks are sourced from imported sugar rather than placing undue pressure on domestic stocks.

Retail sugar prices declined by 10%

Retail sugar prices have declined by around 10% from their peak (Rs. 65 in August to Rs. 58.50). However, ex-mill prices have already declined by nearly 25%. The Government observed that the slower decline in retail prices indicates that the benefit of the reduction in ex-mill prices has not yet been fully transmitted through the supply chain to the consumer.

In a joint meeting held today with representatives of ISMA, the National Federation of Cooperative Sugar Factories and sugar trade, Secretary, Department of Food and Public Distribution, underlined that the reduction in ex-mill prices has not yet been reflected fully in retail prices.

The Government today made a strong appeal to the sugar trade, wholesalers and retailers to immediately pass on the benefit of the significant reduction in ex-mill sugar prices to consumers, emphasising that the decline in retail prices must keep pace with the correction already achieved at the mill level. The Government called upon the entire sugar value chain to collectively ensure that sugar and sugar-based products remain affordable and within the reach of consumers during the forthcoming festivals.

The Secretary emphasised that the farmer and the consumer are the two central pillars of India’s sugar policy. The Government has consistently worked to balance the interests of sugarcane farmers with the need to maintain stable and reasonable sugar prices for consumers. From October 1, 2026, with the commencement of the new sugar season, sugarcane farmers will receive the increased Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) of ₹365 per quintal. The Government has been increasing FRP every year to ensure remunerative returns to sugarcane farmers while maintaining balance in the sugar sector.

The Government will continue to closely monitor the availability and prices of sugar in the domestic market and take appropriate measures, as necessary, to ensure adequate availability of sugar to consumers as well as the requirements of the food processing and other industries.

2311955.title: Creative Economy is Emerging as India’s Next Growth Frontier, Offering New Opportunities for Young Indians: Dr. L. Murugan
2311955.body_html:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Creative Economy is Emerging as India’s Next Growth Frontier, Offering New Opportunities for Young Indians: Dr. L. Murugan
AVGC Sector Expected to Require Nearly 2 million Skilled Professionals by 2030, Opening New Avenues for Youth
Government Supports Indian Institute of Creative Technologies and AVGC Creator Labs to Equip Youth with Future-Ready Skills
Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 2:39PM by PIB Delhi

Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting and Minister of State for Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. L. Murugan, today attended the Opening Ceremony and delivered the Inaugural Address at the Jindal Policy Conclave on the theme “Law, Policy, and the Creative Economy” at O.P. Jindal Global University.

Addressing the young participants, Dr. Murugan highlighted the rapid growth of India’s creative economy, driven by ideas, imagination, culture, innovation and intellectual property. He said that sectors including film, music, gaming, animation, design, publishing, advertising and digital content are creating new opportunities for employment and entrepreneurship.

Dr. Murugan noted that the creative economy contributes 3.1 per cent to global GDP and 6.2 per cent of global employment, with an estimated 57 million Indians already working in cultural and creative occupations. India’s media and entertainment economy stands at ₹2.5 trillion.

Highlighting opportunities for young Indians, he said the AVGC sector alone is expected to require nearly 2 million skilled professionals by 2030. The Government has announced support for the Indian Institute of Creative Technologies and AVGC Creator Labs in 15,000 schools and 500 colleges to prepare youth for emerging opportunities.

Dr. Murugan also emphasised that the growth of the creative economy must be supported by appropriate legal and policy frameworks, including copyright protection, fair compensation for creators and responsible use of artificial intelligence. He urged young people to question assumptions and institutions with respect, reason and evidence and contribute their ideas and skills towards building a Viksit Bharat by 2047.

2311941.title: CGST Delhi South officers bust firm in fraudulent availment of ITC involving over Rs. 25.22 crore; proprietor arrested
2311941.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
CGST Delhi South officers bust firm in fraudulent availment of ITC involving over Rs. 25.22 crore; proprietor arrested
Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 2:26PM by PIB Delhi

As part of its ongoing enforcement drive against fraudulent Input Tax Credit (ITC) claims, the officers of Anti-Evasion Branch, Central Goods & Services Tax (CGST), Delhi South Commissionerate, has arrested a proprietor of a firm engaged in trading of iron and steel goods in a case involving fraudulent availment, utilisation and passing on of inadmissible ITC aggregating to over Rs. 25.22 crore through bogus invoices of approximately Rs. 140.14 crore.

Investigation revealed that the firm had availed inadmissible ITC on the basis of invoices issued by multiple firms, several of which were found to be non-existent, non-functional, suspended or cancelled. Field verification also established that certain suppliers had no genuine business activity at their declared places of business.

Further inquiry established that ITC was availed without actual receipt of goods and was also passed on to various recipients through invoices issued without corresponding supply of goods.

Based on the evidence gathered during investigation and statements recorded under Section 70 of the CGST Act, 2017, the accused was arrested on 17.09.2026 under Section 69 of the CGST Act, 2017 and produced before the Patiala House Court, which remanded him to judicial custody for 14 days.

Further investigation in the case is under progress.

2311937.title: Union Minister Of State Shri B. L. Verma Says Central Government Committed To ‘Vanchiton Ko Variyata’ - Giving Priority To The Deprived
2311937.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Union Minister Of State Shri B. L. Verma Says Central Government Committed To ‘Vanchiton Ko Variyata’ - Giving Priority To The Deprived
PPE Kits Distributed Among 40 Sewer, Septic Tank Workers, 30 Waste Pickers;  Ayushman Cards To 31 Safai Mitras, Keys Of Auto-Rickshaws To 06 Safai Mitras In Budaoun Uttar Pradesh
Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 2:08PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B. L. Verma has said that Central Government is committed to ‘Vanchiton Ko Variyata’ - giving priority to the deprived - by ensuring that people who have historically remained underserved or overlooked receive the assistance and support to which they are entitled.

Addressing the gathering in connection with the Swachhata Hi Seva campaign in Budaun, Uttar Pradesh, with the objective of promoting the message, ‘Honour for Safai Mitras, Resolve for Swachh Bharat’, the Minister highlighted the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme, which seeks to ensure the dignity and safety of sanitation workers and empower them socially and economically.

Shri Verma said that such initiatives focussing on those at the margins, reflects the Government's broader vision of Viksit Bharat, in which every citizen has an opportunity to contribute to and benefit from India's development journey.

The Minister symbolically presented PPE kits to 40 sewer and septic tank workers and 30 waste pickers. In addition, Ayushman cards were also distributed among 31 Safai Mitras, while keys of auto-rickshaws were handed over to six Safai Mitras.

The Minister informed that 90,157 sewer and septic tank workers have been profiled under the Scheme including 87,078 receiving Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kits with 76,920 covered under health insurance.

The Minister further stated that over 5 Lakh (5,00,013) waste pickers have been profiled, of whom 3,15,593 have been validated. He said a total of 1,79,269 waste pickers have been provided PPE kits. In Budaun, 146 sewer and septic tank workers and 339 waste pickers have been validated through the profiling process, he added.

Shri Prabhat Kumar Singh, Managing Director, National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) also spoke on the occasion.

Among those present were Shri Rajeev Singh, Member of the Legislative Assembly, Dataganj; Shri Harish Chandra, Member of the Legislative Assembly, Bilsi; Shri Vagish Pathak, Member of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council and Smt. Varsha Yadav, Chairperson, Zila Panchayat, Budaun.

2311896.body_html:
Ministry of Steel
CVC Organises Training of Trainers Programme on Master Circulars and Vigilance Manual 2026 for Vigilance Officers of South Zone
Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 1:02PM by PIB Delhi

The Vigilance Department of NMDC Limited co-hosted the Training of Trainers Programme conducted by the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) on 17 September 2026 at Hyderabad on “Master Circulars and Vigilance Manual 2026” for Vigilance Officers of organisations in South Zone.

The programme was virtually addressed by the Chief Guest, Shri Praveen Kumar Sinha, Former Special Director, CBI, who emphasised the significance of the CVC Master Circulars and the need for revision of the Vigilance Manual. He also highlighted the importance of rotation of personnel holding sensitive posts as an important preventive vigilance measure.


The occasion was graced by Shri Rajiv Verma, Consultant, CVC; Shri Ajai Kumar Verma, Director, CVC; and Shri Arvind Kumar, OSD, CVC, along with Ms. Spurthi Reddy, CVO, MIDHANI & BDL; Shri P. Krishna Kumar, CVO, ECIL; and Shri C. Neelakanta Reddy, CVO, NMDC Limited.

The distinguished speakers from the CVC provided an overview of the Vigilance Manual 2026, highlighting the key changes and their implications for vigilance administration. They also elaborated on the recently issued CVC Master Circulars, covering their important provisions and practical relevance. The sessions were highly interactive, with the experts addressing participants’ queries and offering valuable clarifications through insightful discussions.

Around 75 Vigilance Officers and representatives from organizations of South Zone participated in the programme. The sessions enhanced participants’ understanding of the updated vigilance framework and provided practical insights to promote consistency in vigilance practices and strengthen institutional capacity.


The CVO, NMDC, emphasised the importance of the CVC Master Circulars and the Vigilance Manual 2026 for vigilance functionaries, highlighting the need for a thorough understanding of their provisions and their effective implementation in vigilance functions.

The HOD, Vigilance, extended sincere gratitude to all the distinguished speakers for sharing their valuable knowledge and experience, and to the participants for their enthusiastic participation, attentive listening and meaningful engagement, which contributed significantly to making the programme highly interactive and enriching.

The programme served as an important platform for knowledge sharing, capacity building and dissemination of updated vigilance manual and master circulars, reinforcing the commitment of participating PSUs towards transparency, probity and effective vigilance administration. The programme concluded with the rendition of the National Anthem and the National Song.

2311874.title: 25th Meeting of SCO Ministers Responsible for Economic and Foreign Trade Activities Held in Tajikistan
2311874.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
25th Meeting of SCO Ministers Responsible for Economic and Foreign Trade Activities Held in Tajikistan
India highlights three pillars of ‘Security, Connectivity and Opportunity’ for international trade
Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 12:43PM by PIB Delhi

The 25th Meeting of Ministers of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Member States Responsible for Foreign Economic and Trade Activities was held in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on 17 September 2026.

The Meeting reviewed ongoing cooperation among SCO Member States in the areas of economic and trade activities and exchanged views on measures to further deepen trade and economic cooperation within the SCO framework.

In his intervention on behalf of India, Shri Yashvir Singh, highlighted the significant economic potential of the SCO and the importance of translating this potential into tangible outcomes through increased intra-SCO trade, lower trade costs, resilient supply chains and enhanced connectivity.

Referring to the vision articulated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi at the SCO Summit in Bishkek, India highlighted the three pillars of Security, Connectivity and Opportunity. India underscored their economic significance, particularly in strengthening supply-chain resilience, developing efficient and trusted connectivity, and expanding opportunities for businesses through greater market access.

India emphasised the important role of trade facilitation and digitalisation in reducing the cost and time associated with trade. In this context, India highlighted the need for simplified customs procedures, paperless trade and electronic exchange of documents, alongside stronger multimodal connectivity and reduced transit times.

India also called for greater cooperation among SCO Member States to diversify and strengthen supply chains in strategic and emerging sectors, including agriculture, critical minerals, pharmaceuticals, manufacturing and electronics. The potential for enhanced cooperation in energy security, renewable energy and green hydrogen was also highlighted.

Recognising the importance of enabling smaller businesses to participate more effectively in regional and global trade, India underscored the role of digital payments, cross-border payments and accessible trade finance, particularly for MSMEs and start-ups. India further called for greater participation of SCO economies in global value chains and reiterated its commitment to an open, inclusive and rules-based multilateral trading system, with the WTO at its core.

The Ministers adopted the ‘Statement of the Ministers of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Member States Responsible for Foreign Economic and Foreign Trade Activity’.

The Ministers agreed on the ‘Action Plan for 2026–2030 for the Implementation of the Programme of Multilateral Trade and Economic Cooperation of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Member States’ for its further approval by the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) of the SCO Member States.

The Ministers also approved the ‘Regulations on the Special Working Group of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Member States on the Development of the Creative Economy’.

The Ministers took note of the information provided by the representative of the SCO Business Council regarding the activities of the Council. They also took note of the information provided by the Tajik side on the work of the SCO Consortium of Economic Analytical Centres.

The Ministers noted that the next Ministerial Meeting will be held in 2027 in the Republic of Uzbekistan.

2311871.title: Progress and preparation for Special Campaign 6.0 by Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
2311871.body_html:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
Progress and preparation for Special Campaign 6.0 by Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 12:33PM by PIB Delhi

The Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters is being organized annually since 2021. To sustain the momentum, the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) along with its attached, subordinate offices and Autonomous Body recorded significant achievements under the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) during November 2025 – August 2026 monitored monthly through SCDPM portal: The campaign resulted in :

  • Review of 5617 files (both physical and e- files)
  • Weeding of 467 physical files
  • Closure of 4680 e-files
  • Conduct of 61 cleanliness campaigns across the country
  • Disposal of Public Grievances :426
  • Disposal of Public Grievances Appeals : 65
  • Revenue generated by scrap disposal: Rs 34,105/-
  • In addition, substantial focus was laid on the disposal of PMO references, Parliamentary assurances and State Government references.

The Government of India has launched Special Campaign 6.0 from 2nd to 31st October 2026. The campaign will focus on “Effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste” across field offices. The campaign is being organized in two phases: the Preparatory Phase (15th – 30th September 2026) and the Implementation Phase (2nd – 31st October 2026) which emphasize on institutionalizing Swachhata and minimizing pendency in offices involving identification of pending references from the PMO, VIPs, State Governments and Parliament, assess the volume of redundant materials to be disposed and finalize the procedures for their disposal, identification of effective collection and segregation of e-waste as per guidelines of MoEFCC for target setting for the forthcoming implementation phase, along with strengthening record and space management practices.

Building on the achievements of previous years, the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) along with its attached office, subordinate offices including field offices and autonomous body, is fully geared up to roll out the Special Campaign 6.0 and committed to actively participate in Special Campaign 6.0.

2311843.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
Union Minister for Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Inaugurates Renovated Guna Head Post Office in Madhya Pradesh
Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 11:49AM by PIB Delhi

The renovated Guna Head Post Office was inaugurated on 17th September 2026 by Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Hon’ble Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region. The inauguration marks an important step towards modernising postal infrastructure and providing more citizen-centric services.

 

The renovation and look-and-feel improvement of Guna Head Post Office has been undertaken at a cost of approximately ₹38 lakh, in accordance with the design guidelines of the School of Planning and Architecture (SPA), New Delhi, under the Department of Posts’ initiative for modernisation of post offices across the country.

The renovated Head Post Office now presents a modern and improved environment for citizens availing postal and financial services. The upgraded infrastructure is aimed at making services more convenient, accessible and customer-friendly, while providing a better experience to the people of Guna and the surrounding areas.

Guna Head Post Office serves a large population of the district and, with its modernised infrastructure, will continue to provide reliable, accessible and citizen-centric postal and financial services.

During the programme, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia appreciated the services being provided by the Department of Posts in the region and the efforts being undertaken to modernise the postal network. He said that post offices equipped with modern facilities would give renewed momentum to postal services and help provide better and quality services to citizens. He also highlighted the well-organised token system introduced at the renovated post office, which will enable customers to avail services in an orderly manner without having to wait in crowded queues. A digital display screen has also been installed to provide information on the timelines for various services. For instance, a duplicate passbook can now be issued within one day.

The Hon’ble Minister also highlighted the digital transformation of postal services and noted that the expansion of digital technology has reduced the need for citizens to visit post offices repeatedly for several services. Through the Dak Sewa and Dak Mitra apps, citizens can access a range of postal services from the convenience of their homes, making postal services more accessible, faster and citizen-centric.

The inauguration of the renovated Guna Head Post Office represents another step towards the Department of Posts’ broader efforts in modernising postal infrastructure, expanding services, strengthening digital delivery and enhancing the capabilities of its workforce. The upgraded facility is expected to further improve the delivery of postal and financial services to citizens in Guna and the surrounding areas.

2311836.title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported death of a four-year-old girl after falling into an uncovered manhole near her house in Palwal, Haryana
2311836.body_html:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported death of a four-year-old girl after falling into an uncovered manhole near her house in Palwal, Haryana
Issues notices to the Deputy Commissioner and the Superintendent of Police, Palwal for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 11:43AM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that a four-year-old girl died after falling into an uncovered manhole while playing near her house in Palwal, Haryana on 14th September 2026. Reportedly, despite several complaints by the local residents to the concerned authorities, the manhole remained uncovered.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the media report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued notices to the Deputy Commissioner and the Superintendent of Police, Palwal, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks. The report is expected to include the status of the investigation and compensation, if any, paid to the next of kin of the deceased.

According to the media report, carried out on 16th September 2026, the victim girls' family and local residents found her inside the uncovered manhole and took her in critical condition to the District Civil Hospital, where the doctors declared her dead.

2311827.title: Indian Railways Approves ₹493 Crore for 38.21 km New Rail Line between Mukutban (Adilabad) and Gadchandur
2311827.body_html:
Ministry of Railways
Indian Railways Approves ₹493 Crore for 38.21 km New Rail Line between Mukutban (Adilabad) and Gadchandur
New Line to Provide Shorter Rail Route, Strengthen Freight Connectivity and Support Industrial & Mining Development
Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 11:23AM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards strengthening regional rail connectivity and facilitating faster and more efficient movement of passengers and freight, Indian Railways has approved the construction of the 38.21 km new rail line between Mukutban (Adilabad) and Gadchandur in South Central Railway at a cost of ₹493 crore.

Strengthening Connectivity to Industrial and Mining Centres

Mukutban in Yavatmal district and Gadchandur in Chandrapur district are important industrial and mining centres, serving several cement plants, coal mines of Western Coalfields Ltd. and nearby limestone mines. The new rail line will strengthen rail connectivity to these industrial clusters and facilitate more efficient movement of freight.

Shorter Route to Improve Freight Movement and Decongest Existing Network

The new rail line will provide a shorter and more efficient rail route, reducing travel distance, transportation time and associated costs. It will also provide an alternative route to decongest the existing Wardha-Manikgarh section, supporting smoother movement of freight traffic.

As per the Detailed Project Report, the project is expected to support 6.08 MTPA of freight traffic, along with two MEMU trains in each direction per day after commissioning. The freight traffic is expected to include coal and coke, cement, sponge iron, metal scrap, iron & steel, fertilisers and foodgrains, among other commodities.

Direct Connectivity to Majri-Nanded Route and Key Destinations

The new line will provide direct connectivity between the coal and cement cluster and the Majri-Nanded route, facilitating shorter leads for coal, cement and RMSP traffic towards Jalna, Parbhani, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and other destinations in Maharashtra and Karnataka.

Reducing Dependence on Congested Balharshah-Nagpur Route

The project will reduce dependence on the congested Balharshah-Nagpur High-Density Network (HDN) route, while improving rail connectivity to the relatively less-connected areas of Yavatmal and Chandrapur districts. This will support industrial and economic development in the region through enhanced rail infrastructure.

Strengthening Regional Rail Infrastructure

The new rail line will add capacity to the regional railway network, facilitate movement of essential commodities and provide an additional rail corridor for growing freight and passenger requirements. The project is expected to contribute to more efficient utilisation of the existing railway network while supporting industrial and regional economic activity.

*****

2311826.title: Indian Railways Approves Doubling of Chouk-Karjat Railway Section in Maharashtra at a Cost of ₹497 Crore
2311826.body_html:
Ministry of Railways
Indian Railways Approves Doubling of Chouk-Karjat Railway Section in Maharashtra at a Cost of ₹497 Crore
10.86 km Doubling Project to Enhance Passenger and Freight Capacity on the Panvel-Chouk-Karjat Route
Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 11:21AM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards augmenting railway capacity and improving train operations in Maharashtra, Indian Railways has approved the doubling of the Chouk-Karjat railway section (10.86 km) of Central Railway at a cost of ₹497 crore. The project has been approved under the umbrella works for doubling, tripling, quadrupling, flyover and bypass works aimed at augmenting the capacity of the railway network.

The Chouk-Karjat section forms part of the Panvel-Chouk-Karjat route, which is an important corridor for both passenger and freight movement. The doubling of the section will provide additional capacity on the existing single-line stretch and help improve the movement of trains.

On completion of the project, the section is expected to facilitate five additional passenger trains in each direction per day. The project is also expected to support additional freight traffic of 18.35 Million Tonnes Per Annum (MTPA). It will also help reduce detention of freight trains.

The doubling of the Chouk-Karjat section reflects Indian Railways’ continued focus on strengthening railway infrastructure, enhancing capacity and improving passenger and freight movement.

2311804.title: Ministry of Culture organises ‘Aashirwad Ka Diya’ programme at Purana Qila on the birthday of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi
2311804.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
Ministry of Culture organises ‘Aashirwad Ka Diya’ programme at Purana Qila on the birthday of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi
Under the leadership of the Prime Minister, public trust has been strengthened in the country and efforts have been made to take development forward with public participation: Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat
Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 10:29AM by PIB Delhi

On the occasion of the birthday of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Ministry of Culture organised the ‘Aashirwad Ka Diya’ programme at Purana Qila, New Delhi, on 17th September 2026. Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat inaugurated the programme by lighting the Aashirwad Ka Diya, organised under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan with the chant of “Bharat Mata Ki Jai”.

In his address, Union Minister Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat said that the Aashirwad Ka Diya is not just a lamp, but a symbol of the power of people's blessings, service, gratitude and the resolve for a Viksit Bharat. He said that in Indian culture, the diya gives the message of burning itself to spread light in others' lives, dispelling darkness and paving the way for public welfare. In this spirit, this lamp is also a symbol of collective resolve towards service to the nation.

Wishing the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on his birthday, the Union Minister said that his public life has been dedicated to national interest and public service. He said that from his childhood till today, in whatever role he has got an opportunity to work, he has worked with full dedication and a spirit of service, keeping the nation supreme. From taking charge as the Chief Minister of Gujarat to leading the country as the Prime Minister, his commitment to national service, public welfare and development has remained constant, he added.

Sharing his experience of working with the Prime Minister, Shri Shekhawat said that getting the opportunity to work with the Prime Minister has been an honourable experience of his public life. He said that he has seen Shri Narendra Modi not only as a Prime Minister, but as a dedicated worker, seeker, ascetic and organizer. He said that the Prime Minister inspires people at every level through his conduct, working style and guidance and considers public office not as prestige, but as a medium of responsibility and service.

The Union Minister said that the Prime Minister's working style is based on outcome-oriented governance. Schemes are reviewed not just on the basis of processes or data, but on the basis of their actual impact on society and the change reaching the last person, he said. Union Minister added that the Prime Minister's clear view is that merely moving a file forward is not the completion of work, but the public-welfare results arising from it is the real yardstick of good governance.

Shri Shekhawat said that after 2014, India has experienced a new journey of development and good governance. He said that under the leadership of the Prime Minister, public trust has been strengthened in the country and efforts have been made to take development forward with public participation. He also said that the Prime Minister believes that “heritage and development” are not contradictory to each other, but complementary to each other and both have an equal role in building a Viksit Bharat.

In this context, the Union Minister said that the Ministry of Culture is working with the resolve of “Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi” under the guidance of the Prime Minister. He said that India's classical, folk and traditional cultural traditions are invaluable heritage of our civilizational consciousness and their preservation, promotion and dissemination to the new generation is the priority of the Ministry. He also said that only a society inspired by its heritage can move forward with confidence and pride towards the goal of Viksit Bharat.

In his address, Shri Shekhawat mentioned the recently held BRICS Summit and said that India's role at the global level and the growing trust of the world in India reflects the country's decisive leadership and its commitment to national interest. He said that even in difficult situations and challenges, India has established its effective role before the world community by keeping national interest’s paramount.

Artists and students of Sangeet Natak Akademi, Kathak Kendra, National School of Drama, Lalit Kala Akademi and Zonal Cultural Centres gave presentations based on Indian classical and cultural traditions at the event.  After the programme, the Union Minister interacted with artists, students, representatives of the National Culture Fund, Adopt a Heritage initiative and other stakeholders and appreciated their contribution in the preservation and promotion of Indian cultural heritage.

The programme concluded with the collective lighting of the Aashirwad Ka Diya. On this occasion, the resolve for service, culture, nation-building and Viksit Bharat 2047 in Amrit Kaal was reiterated.

***
